items.title: Kankan : poignardée au ventre à 9 mois de grossesse par la »maitresse » de son mari, une femme perd son bébé
items.description: Une scène d’une rare violence s’est produite mardi 8 septembre 2026, dans le quartier de Sènkèfara, relevant de la commune urbaine de Kankan. Une femme enceinte de neuf mois a été agressée à l’arme blanche, alors qu’elle était arrivée au terme de sa grossesse. Selon ses proches, le bébé est décédé à la suite des complications liées à cette agression. D’après les informations recueillies auprès de la famille, la victime aurait reçu un coup de couteau au niveau du ventre. Elle a été rapidement transportée à l’hôpital régional de Kankan, où elle a été prise en charge par les services médicaux. Très affectée par la situation, Fanta Condé, mère de la victime, affirme avoir appris l’agression par téléphone. « J’étais à la maison lorsque j’ai reçu un appel m’informant que la copine du mari de ma fille était partie la poignarder au ventre. Je ne sais pas pour quelle raison. Pourtant, ma fille était enceinte de neuf mois. Elle ne connaissait pas cette femme, et moi non plus. Je remercie Dieu parce que ma fille n’est pas décédée grâce à la prise en charge des médecins », témoigne-t-elle. Selon la famille, l’agression aurait été commise par une femme présentée comme entretenant une relation avec le conjoint de la victime. Cette version n’a toutefois pas été confirmée, à ce stade, par les autorités judiciaires. Toujours selon les proches et des sources hospitalières, la victime aurait présenté des complications, notamment des saignements, à la suite de l’agression. Le corps du nouveau-né est actuellement conservé à la morgue de l’hôpital régional de Kankan. La famille affirme avoir entrepris des démarches pour sa récupération, mais le procureur de la République près le Tribunal de première instance de Kankan n’aurait pas encore autorisé sa restitution. Contacté par notre rédaction dans la journée du mercredi 9 septembre, le procureur de la République près le Tribunal de première instance de Kankan, Fodé Bintou Kéita, a indiqué que le dossier devait être transmis à son parquet. Il a précisé ne pas l’avoir encore reçu au moment de nos échanges. Une source proche du dossier affirme par ailleurs que la femme mise en cause ferait actuellement l’objet de poursuites dans le cadre de l’enquête judiciaire. Contacté par notre rédaction, le service de la maternité de l’hôpital régional de Kankan n’a pas souhaité communiquer sur cette affaire, en l’absence d’autorisation de communiquer sur ce type de situation. À ce stade, les circonstances exactes de l’agression ainsi que les responsabilités éventuelles restent à déterminer par l’enquête judiciaire. Saisi du dossier dans la soirée de ce mercredi 9 septembre, le parquet près le Tribunal de première instance de Kankan devrait, dans les prochaines heures, apporter davantage d’éclaircissements sur les circonstances de cette affaire.

items.title: Branchement à l’ONEA: ce n’est pas 120 000 FCFA
items.description: Dans un communiqué, ce mercredi 9 septembre 2026, l’Office national de l’eau et de l’assainissement (ONEA) donne des Précisions sur les conditions et le coût du branchement. Des informations faisaient état d’un montant de 120 000 FCFA contre 30 500 FCFA précédemment. COMMUNIQUÉ Précisions sur les conditions et le coût du branchement à l’ONEA Depuis quelques jours, des informations relatives à une évolution du coût du branchement à l’Office national de l’eau et de l’assainissement (ONEA), faisant état d’un montant de 120 000 FCFA contre 30 500 FCFA précédemment, circulent dans les médias et suscitent de nombreuses interrogations parmi les usagers. L’ONEA tient à apporter les précisions suivantes : À ce jour, les usagers sollicitant un branchement à l’ONEA acquittent 30 500 FCFA au titre des frais d’établissement de la police d’abonnement, correspondant à une caution remboursable en cas de sa résiliation, conformément aux conditions actuellement en vigueur. Il convient de préciser que ce montant ne constitue pas le coût de réalisation du branchement. Les travaux et équipements nécessaires à la réalisation du branchement sont actuellement pris en charge par l’État à travers le Ministère en charge de l’Eau. Ainsi, le coût du branchement n’est, à ce stade, pas directement supporté par l’usager. Dans le souci d’assurer la pérennité du service public de l’eau potable et de renforcer la capacité de l’ONEA à faire face à l’évolution de ses charges d’exploitation et d’investissement, ses services compétents ont engagé une réflexion sur la structure tarifaire de l’eau ainsi que sur les conditions économiques et financières de réalisation des branchements. Cette réflexion vise notamment à rechercher un juste équilibre entre, d’une part, la viabilité financière de l’ONEA et, d’autre part, la préservation de la politique nationale d’accès universel et équitable à l’eau potable, qui demeure une priorité du Gouvernement. Toute éventuelle évolution des conditions et du coût du branchement doit, à cet effet, être appréciée dans le cadre global de cette réflexion et intervenir conformément aux procédures et aux textes réglementaires applicables. L’ONEA tient à préciser qu’aucune décision réglementaire définitive de la part des autorités compétentes n’a, à ce stade, consacré une modification du coût du branchement à 120 000 FCFA. En conséquence, l’application anticipée du montant de 120 000 FCFA par les services de l’ONEA est suspendue jusqu’à l’aboutissement des réflexions engagées et à l’adoption des textes et décisions réglementaires nécessaires à l’encadrement de toute éventuelle évolution des conditions et tarifs de branchement. Dans l’attente, les conditions et le tarif actuellement en vigueur demeurent applicables et les dispositions qui ont été mises en œuvre à titre transitoire sont, par conséquent, suspendues. Pour les usagers ayant déjà acquitté un montant supérieur aux conditions actuellement en vigueur, les modalités de régularisation ou de remboursement du différentiel seront communiquées par l’ONEA dans les meilleurs délais, conformément aux dispositions qui seront arrêtées à cet effet. L’ONEA comprend les préoccupations exprimées par les usagers et tient à les rassurer sur sa volonté de conduire cette réflexion dans un esprit de transparence, d’équité et de préservation de l’accessibilité du service public de l’eau potable. L’ONEA réaffirme son engagement à garantir un service public de l’eau potable accessible, de qualité, durable et financièrement soutenable au bénéfice de l’ensemble des populations. Il remercie les usagers pour leur compréhension et leur confiance. ONEA L’article Branchement à l’ONEA: ce n'est pas 120 000 FCFA est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: China Wants Citizens to Report ‘Illegal’ Religious Practice
items.description: Click to expand Image The eight members of Zion Church who remain detained. Top from left to right: Gao Yingjia, Wang Cong, Wang Lin, Lin ShuchengBottom from left to right: Wu Qiuyu, Liu Zhenbin, Yin Huibin, Wang Zhong © Private Chinese lawyer Ruth Wang fled to Taiwan on September 2 after authorities threatened to shut down her law firm. Her offense? Representing members of China’s Zion Church, a prominent underground Protestant congregation. While founding pastor Ezra Jin was freed from custody in July following high-level US intervention, eight other church members have remained wrongfully detained since their October 2025 arrests. Chinese leader Xi Jinping launched his “Sinicization of religion” policy in 2016, which included government regulations tightening controls over religious life. Beijing is not only punishing people for independent religious practice but also those defending their rights. Recently, authorities have continued to tighten surveillance over religious activities. In the first half of 2026 alone, more than a dozen cities across the country introduced measures encouraging or rewarding people to report religious activities the government labels “illegal.” The reporting rules are sweeping. In February, authorities in Honghe prefecture, Yunnan province, listed 35 categories of reportable “illegal religious activity.” These include holding collective religious activities or ceremonies in private homes or other “unapproved” venues, clergy preaching through livestreams or WeChat groups, distributing religious materials in public places, and organizing religious education or training without official approval. Authorities in Haidong, Qinghai province, extended reporting obligations to businesses, ordering hotels and travel agencies to screen the events they host and report any “suspicious situation.” Almost all of the new regulations offer informants rewards. In Chengdu, Sichuan province, authorities are offering up to 800 RMB (US$120) for verified tips about vaguely defined “illegal” religious conduct. These measures, which appear to build upon similar ones in Xinjiang since 2013 and in Guangdong since 2019, send yet another chilling signal to Christians, Muslims, and Tibetan Buddhists in China who have faced intense pressure to closely reflect and follow Han Chinese culture and Chinese Communist Party ideology. The new measures followed changes to the Public Security Administration Punishment Law, which took effect on January 1. For the first time, the law made “illegal religious activities” grounds for 5 to 15 days of administrative detention. The Chinese government insists that people in China can freely worship. While many people in China continue to practice religion, they can only do so strictly within the authorities’ ever-tightening bounds. That is what “Sinicization” means in practice. Beijing’s claims won’t be taken seriously so long as churchgoers and other religious adherents are being detained for exercising their religious freedom.

items.title: Kamsar érigée en préfecture : le maire Sékou Oumar Sylla salue une décision « historique »
items.description: L’érection de Kamsar en préfecture constitue un tournant majeur pour cette importante localité de la région de Boké. Pour le maire de la commune, Sékou Oumar Sylla, cette décision vient couronner plusieurs décennies de revendications portées par les populations locales. Très ému par cette évolution administrative, cet élu de Kamsar estime que cette décision revêt une dimension particulière pour lui et pour les familles qui ont longtemps milité en faveur de l’accession de la ville au statut de préfecture. « C’est vraiment historique. Moi, je suis très content, plus que tout le monde, parce que nos parents se sont battus à Kamsar ici pour que cette ville soit érigée en préfecture. Certains même ont été enfermés par rapport à ça », a-t-il déclaré. Selon lui, l’aboutissement de cette revendication prend également une dimension personnelle. Il rappelle que certains de ses parents ont participé à cette lutte et se réjouit de voir aujourd’hui Kamsar accéder à ce nouveau statut. « Aujourd’hui, c’est l’un de leurs fils qui est là et qui voit Kamsar érigée en préfecture. En son temps, vraiment, c’est quelque chose que moi, je ne vais jamais oublier, parce que mon nom est gravé dans l’histoire », souligne-t-il. Au-delà de sa satisfaction personnelle, il attribue cette avancée à la mobilisation collective des populations de Kamsar. Il adresse ainsi ses félicitations à l’ensemble des habitants, tout en exprimant sa reconnaissance au président de la République pour cette décision. « Félicitations à tout Kamsar, parce que c’est tout Kamsar qui s’est battu depuis fort longtemps. Aujourd’hui, on ne cesse de remercier le président de la République par rapport à cette grande décision », affirme-t-il. Il formule également des prières en faveur du chef de l’État, souhaitant qu’il dispose de la force nécessaire pour poursuivre la conduite des affaires du pays. Interrogé sur les raisons ayant pu favoriser l’érection de Kamsar en préfecture, notamment l’augmentation de sa population et son poids économique, Sékou Oumar Sylla estime que la localité disposait depuis longtemps de nombreux atouts pour accéder à ce statut. Il rappelle notamment un échange récent avec le Premier ministre, au cours duquel cette question avait été évoquée : « Il y a deux jours, on était face au Premier ministre. C’est ce qu’il nous a dit : Kamsar méritait d’être une préfecture depuis fort longtemps. » Selon le maire, même si des hésitations ont pu exister par le passé, les caractéristiques de Kamsar plaidaient depuis longtemps en faveur de son érection en préfecture. « Peut-être qu’il y avait des hésitations quelque part, mais sinon, comme vous l’avez dit, Kamsar a presque tout pour devenir une préfecture depuis longtemps », a-t-il conclu. Cette nouvelle configuration administrative devrait ainsi renforcer le rôle de Kamsar dans l’organisation territoriale de la Guinée et répondre aux aspirations longtemps exprimées par ses habitants. items.title: JOJ Dakar 2026 : dans les coulisses de la cérémonie de la flamme à Athènes
items.description: À Athènes, les choses sérieuses ont commencé. Ce mercredi, le stade Panathénaïque a accueilli la répétition générale de la cérémonie d’allumage et de remise de la flamme des Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse Dakar 2026. Pendant plus de deux heures, les différents tableaux de cette cérémonie historique ont été répétés, en présence de nombreux officiels sénégalais, dont Ibrahima Wade et Louis Lamotte. Dans ce stade millénaire, berceau symbolique de l’olympisme moderne, la cérémonie respectera le protocole olympique. Elle s’ouvrira par une prestation de jeunes artistes, mêlant tradition et modernité, sur la piste du Panathénaïque. Place ensuite aux hymnes du Sénégal, du Comité international olympique et de la Grèce. L’hymne grec sera interprété par une chanteuse hellénique, accompagnée au violoncelle. Celui du Sénégal sera chanté a cappella par une talentueuse et émergente voix de la musique sénégalaise, dont la puissance donnera une forte intensité à ce moment solennel. Viendra ensuite le temps fort : l’allumage de la flamme olympique. Une séquence hautement symbolique au cours de laquelle la flamme sera extraite du vase olympique avant d’être transmise à la torche. Commencera alors le relais autour de la piste du stade. Un premier relayeur grec ouvrira la marche, avant que la flamme ne passe entre les mains de plusieurs représentants sénégalais. Un basketteur sénégalais bien connu du public donnera le premier relais sénégalais. Il sera suivi par un athlète ayant participé à deux éditions des Jeux olympiques, puis par une jeune nageuse sénégalaise, qui aura l’honneur de poursuivre cette course symbolique. La cérémonie se poursuivra avec les discours des autorités grecques, du Comité international olympique et du Sénégal. Parmi les prises de parole attendues, celle de Mamadou Diagna Ndiaye, président du Comité d’organisation des Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse (JOJ) « Dakar 2026 ». Puis viendra le moment du passage de témoin. La flamme sera remise à Mamadou Diagna Ndiaye, accompagné de Djirèye Clothilde Coly, ministre de la Jeunesse et des Sports, de Baïdy Agne, vice-président du Comité national olympique et sportif sénégalais (CNOSS), ainsi que de l’ensemble de la délégation sénégalaise. Ensemble, ils auront la responsabilité de ramener cette flamme vers le Sénégal. A partir de ce moment, commencera alors son voyage d’Athènes, berceau de l’olympisme, vers Dakar, prochaine capitale mondiale de la jeunesse. Cette flamme allumée ce jeudi 10 septembre 2026 sera chargée d’histoire. En effet, elle est appelée à devenir, dans quelques semaines, le symbole des premiers Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse organisés en Afrique. Moussa DIOP, envoyé spécial à Athènes (Grèce)

items.title: Richard Nii Armah Quaye, Ga Mantse to launch scholarship scheme for Ga-Dangbe students
items.description: Founder and President of RNAQ Foundation, Richard Nii Armah Quaye, in collaboration with the Ga Mantse, King Tackie Teiko Tsuru II, is set to launch a scholarship scheme for Ga-Dangbe students The initiative, scheduled to be officially launched on Monday, September 14, aims to support bright and promising students within the Ga-Dangbe community while promoting unity and encouraging collective investment in the development of the people. The scholarship scheme forms part of a broader vision to create greater educational opportunities for young Ga-Dangbe people and ensure that financial challenges do not prevent deserving students from pursuing their education. The initiative also seeks to encourage individuals and institutions within the Ga-Dangbe community to contribute to the development of future scholars, professionals and leaders. According to Mr Armah Quaye, the scholarship is intended to go beyond providing financial assistance to individual beneficiaries and serve as part of a long-term effort to build a stronger and more united Ga-Dangbe community. The initiative is also expected to promote a culture of giving back, with successful members of the community encouraged to invest in opportunities that benefit the next generation. Mr Armah Quaye, who is from the Ga-Dangbe community, is leading the initiative as part of efforts to reinvest in the community and support its development. The launch will bring together traditional leaders, community members and other stakeholders to highlight the importance of education and collective responsibility in shaping the future of the Ga-Dangbe people. He believes that investing in education will help produce a new generation of Ga-Dangbe scholars, professionals and leaders capable of contributing to the development of the community and Ghana as a whole.

items.title: Guinée–Sierra Leone : immigration, frontières et coopération au cœur des échanges à Conakry
items.description: Le Premier ministre, chef du gouvernement, Amadou Oury Bah, a reçu ce mercredi 9 septembre 2026, à la Primature, le vice-président de la République de Sierra Leone, Dr Mohamed Juldeh Jalloh, en visite de travail à Conakry. Les échanges entre les deux responsables ont porté sur plusieurs sujets d’intérêt commun, notamment les suites du drame de Dar Es Salam, les questions migratoires, la sécurisation des frontières ainsi que le renforcement de la coopération économique et sécuritaire entre la Guinée et la Sierra Leone. À sa sortie de la rencontre, le Premier ministre guinéen a rappelé les liens historiques, géographiques et humains entre les deux pays, tout en saluant la démarche de Freetown. « Membres de la délégation sierra-léonaise, c’est un honneur et un plaisir pour la Guinée de recevoir cette délégation d’un pays frère, d’un pays voisin, et d’un pays avec lequel, récemment, on a été endeuillé suite à l’éboulement de la décharge de Dar Es Salam. Donc, au nom du président Doumbouya, je vous souhaite la bienvenue. Cette rencontre augure de bonnes perspectives de la résolution, de la manière la plus pacifique, la plus conviviale et fraternelle, des préoccupations qui existent entre les deux pays qui sont des voisins, qui sont liés par l’histoire, la géographie et la communauté de destin. » Les questions migratoires et la sécurisation des frontières ont occupé une place importante dans les discussions. « Nous avons abordé cette suite qui concerne beaucoup plus les populations elles-mêmes : le deuil ensuite, la question de l’immigration et les questions relatives à la stabilisation et la sécurisation des frontières entre la Guinée et la Sierra Leone », a expliqué Amadou Oury Bah. Ces échanges s’inscrivent dans le prolongement du sommet extraordinaire des chefs d’État de l’Union du fleuve Mano, tenu à Conakry le 16 mars dernier. « Bien entendu, tout cela s’inscrit dans la logique de la rencontre du sommet extraordinaire des chefs d’État de l’Union du Fleuve Mano qui avait eu lieu à Conakry le 16 mars dernier », a rappelé le chef du gouvernement. Selon lui, la visite du vice-président sierra-léonais devrait contribuer à donner un nouvel élan à cette organisation régionale. « Donc cette visite de travail concourt à redynamiser l’Union du Fleuve Mano, qui mérite d’ici la fin de l’année, qu’au point de vue institutionnel et au point de vue organisationnel, d’être relancée. » Freetown présente ses condoléances après le drame de Dar Es Salam Prenant à son tour la parole, le vice-président sierra-léonais, accompagné d’une délégation de quatre personnes, a d’abord remercié les autorités guinéennes pour l’accueil réservé à sa délégation ainsi que pour leur participation à la cérémonie d’inauguration de la politique étrangère de la Guinée. Dr Mohamed Juldeh Jalloh a ensuite indiqué que sa venue à Conakry était également motivée par la volonté du président Julius Maada Bio, du gouvernement et du peuple sierra-léonais d’exprimer leur compassion aux familles endeuillées par l’éboulement de Dar Es Salam. « D’abord, avant tout, je suis venu avec une délégation pour porter un message de compassion au nom du président Julius Maada Bio, du gouvernement et du peuple sierra-léonais. Je présente les condoléances sincères aux familles des victimes, des victimes du drame qui s’est déroulé dans la nuit du 22 au 23 août à Dar Es Salam. » Le vice-président sierra-léonais a également salué la réaction des autorités guinéennes dans la gestion des opérations de secours. « Je tiens à rappeler que parmi les victimes, les ressortissants sierra-léonais ont subi cette perte humaine… Je voudrais utiliser cette plateforme pour remercier chaleureusement le gouvernement guinéen, ainsi que Son Excellence le président de la République, le général Mamadi Doumbouya, pour la rapidité et l’efficacité des secours qui se sont déployés, ainsi que pour la dignité, de façon sans distinction de nationalité, accordée à toutes les victimes. Cela montre très bien la fraternité qui existe entre nos deux pays, et aussi les Sierra-Léonais n’oublient pas cela. » Au-delà du contexte douloureux lié au drame de Dar Es Salam, les deux délégations ont également évoqué le suivi des engagements pris lors de la réunion des dirigeants de l’espace du fleuve Mano. « Aussi, au-delà de ce moment de recueillement, notre visite s’inscrit dans la logique de notre engagement commun. Comme le Premier ministre vient de l’évoquer, on a aussi profité pour discuter de la façon dont nos deux pays peuvent faire le suivi concret de la réunion des trois chefs d’État qui s’est tenue ici le 16 mars dernier, surtout dans la façon dont on va continuer à travailler pour apaiser les tensions frontalières et aussi renforcer la coopération commune. » Des mesures annoncées prochainement sur l’immigration La question migratoire a également occupé une place importante dans les échanges entre les deux délégations. « Également, on a discuté les questions d’immigration. Ensemble, les deux équipes des deux gouvernements ont pris des mesures qui vont être annoncées très prochainement sur la question de l’immigration », a annoncé Mohamed Juldeh Jalloh. Le vice-président sierra-léonais a par ailleurs annoncé de prochaines discussions entre les ministres chargés du Commerce et de l’Industrie des deux pays. « Et aussi, on a terminé par souligner l’importance de la coopération entre les deux pays, surtout la coopération économique et sécuritaire. Dans les jours et les mois à venir, nos ministres du Commerce et de l’Industrie rendront visite à Conakry pour travailler avec leur homologue, le ministre du Commerce et de l’Industrie, pour pouvoir organiser une foire ou un salon de commerce commun. » Selon lui, cette initiative devrait contribuer davantage à l’intégration entre les deux pays. « Tout ça, ça rentre dans l’intégration. Comme aujourd’hui on vient juste d’inaugurer le document de la politique étrangère, il y a une chose qui nous a remarqués : c’est la politique de bon voisinage. Dans cette logique de politique de bon voisinage, c’est ça qui s’inscrit cette visite », a-t-il déclaré. À l’issue de cette rencontre, Conakry et Freetown affichent ainsi leur volonté de poursuivre le dialogue afin de renforcer leur coopération, d’apaiser les tensions frontalières et de consolider leur politique de bon voisinage. Marie Mayi CISSÉ L’article Guinée–Sierra Leone : immigration, frontières et coopération au cœur des échanges à Conakry est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Julius Emunah parts ways with Hearts of Oak as Managing Director
items.description: Accra Hearts of Oak Managing Director, Julius Ben Emunah has officially announced his resignation from the position, bringing his seven-month tenure at the club to an end. Emunah, who was appointed Managing Director effective February 2, 2026, succeeded Dr Delali Anku-Adiamah. He joined the Phobians after serving as Head of Competitions at the Ghana Football Association. In a farewell message to the club on facebook , Emunah described his decision to resign as a difficult one. “It is with a heavy heart that I announce my decision to resign from my position as Managing Director of our dear Accra Hearts of Oak.” He also expressed gratitude to the club’s Board, led by HRH Togbe Afede XIV, for the confidence placed in him and to the National Chapter Committee (NCC) for their support during his time in office. Despite stepping down as Managing Director, Emunah made it clear that his relationship with the club will continue. “Although I am stepping down from my role, I am not stepping away from the club. I remain a proud and committed supporter and will always be available to serve, assist, or support the club in whatever capacity I can.” he wrote. He added that “I leave the position with immense appreciation and the firm conviction that the club has a bright future ahead.” His appointment in February was part of Hearts of Oak’s push to strengthen its administrative structure, with the club highlighting his nearly decade-long experience in football administration, governance and sports management.

items.title: Weija Dam flooding will persist without political will to relocate residents – NADMO
items.description: The National Disaster Management Organisation (NADMO) says flooding of communities downstream of the Weija Dam will persist unless authorities muster the political will to relocate residents from areas originally designated as buffer zones. Speaking during an assessment of the impact of the flooding on affected communities on Wednesday, September 9, the Greater Accra Regional Director of NADMO, Dennis Nartey, said the areas beneath the dam were deliberately reserved as buffers during the construction of the facility to accommodate excess water whenever the dam reaches high levels. However, he said years of encroachment have significantly reduced the available buffer, leaving downstream communities vulnerable whenever water is released from the dam. “At some point, there will be that political will to do resettlement,” he said. He explained that the buffer zones were designed to provide space for water to flow when the dam is opened, but increasing development in those areas has undermined that arrangement. He added, “When the dam was being built, they took into consideration all these factors and beneath the dam area, those places were to serve as buffers, so that in case the dam had to open, then the water would flow to those areas. But today we have encroached all those areas.” Mr Nartey said NADMO’s immediate responsibility is to reduce the risk to lives and property through public education and early warnings. He assured residents that there was no cause for alarm, saying NADMO had intensified awareness campaigns and identified safer, higher areas where residents could move to in the event of possible flooding. “When we are expecting heavy water level upstream, then we have to advise them. We have identified places that are very high for them, in case of any possible event. NADMO is ready,” he said.

items.title: UMB, 3TREES launch paint outlets across constituencies ahead of Ghana’s 70th anniversary
items.description: Universal Merchant Bank (UMB) and 3TREES Ghana have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) for a paint discount scheme that includes plans to establish a sales outlet in every constituency ahead of Ghana’s 70th independence anniversary. The agreement forms part of the Brighten Ghana Initiative, which will offer discounts ranging from 35 per cent to 55 per cent on exterior all-weather paints, in line with approved specifications. Sales are scheduled to run from October 1, 2026 to March 30, 2027, spanning the country’s anniversary on 6 March 2027. The programme targets individuals, businesses, schools and community organisations undertaking painting and building maintenance projects. Under the initiative’s proposed roadmap, Members of Parliament are expected to support local mobilisation and assist with the establishment of outlets in their constituencies. The planned network is intended to bring participating products closer to communities and support local trade and employment. The outlets remain part of a future rollout, with local availability dependent on their establishment and opening. UMB is participating alongside Strawberry Star and 3TREES Ghana. The bank will serve as the initiative’s Official Banking Partner and Settlement Bank and is developing a dedicated digital payment platform to facilitate purchases of participating paint products. UMB’s Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, Dr. Philip Oti-Mensah, said the bank’s involvement reflected its commitment to supporting national development beyond its core banking services. The initiative links preparations for Ghana’s 70th anniversary with efforts to maintain and improve residential, commercial and community buildings. Its stated objectives combine access to discounted paint with opportunities for constituency-level retail activity. The applicable discount will depend on the eligible product and approved specifications, while customers’ access to local sales outlets will depend on the progress of the constituency rollout.

items.title: CSSPS: Education Ministry orders action against alleged payment demands in Ashanti Region
items.description: The Ministry of Education has directed officials of the Ghana Education Service (GES) in the Ashanti Region to take steps to stop alleged demands for money from parents seeking assistance with the Computerised School Selection and Placement System (CSSPS). The directive comes after some parents in Kumasi alleged that unidentified individuals at the resolution centre were demanding up to GH¢300 to help candidates bypass long queues and fast-track their placement concerns. The allegations have heightened frustration at the centre, with some parents reportedly abandoning the process after spending hours waiting for assistance. Speaking on Joy FM’s Newsnight , the Media Relations Officer at the Ministry of Education, Hashmin Mohammed, said the allegation had not been brought directly to his attention but that the ministry had monitored reports in the media. He said the ministry subsequently “contacted GES officials in the Ashanti Region and the Free Senior High School coordinator overseeing the placement process to ensure that any such practice is stopped.” He stressed that parents are not required to pay anyone for CSSPS placement services. He said the regional officials have been tasked to put measures in place if the reported practice exists and prevent parents from being exploited while seeking assistance with the placement process. items.title: Device Mgt System won’t expose users’ data – NCC
items.description: By Prince Osuagwu The Nigerian Communications Commission, NCC, has allayed fears that its new Device Management System, DMS, designed to strengthen Type Approval compliance for mobile devices in Nigeria, could give the regulator access to users’ personal data and communications. The Commission, in a statement by its Director, Corporate Affairs, Nnenna Ukoha, maintained that the insinuation was unfounded, stressing that the platform was designed solely for device identification and regulatory compliance. The clarification followed concerns over the Commission’s plan to electronically determine the Type Approval compliance of SIM-enabled devices through the DMS, which is being deployed to improve oversight of the country’s communications device ecosystem. According to the NCC, the system will maintain device identification information, including the International Mobile Equipment Identity, IMEI, numbers of devices operating in Nigeria, but will not provide access to the contents of users’ devices or personal communications. The Commission said the initiative is part of efforts to ensure that communications devices imported, sold and used in Nigeria meet applicable technical and regulatory standards. Under Section 132(2) of the Nigerian Communications Act 2003, licensed service and facilities providers, equipment manufacturers and suppliers are required to obtain Type Approval from the Commission before communications equipment can be sold or used in Nigeria. The NCC said the Device Management System would also help identify non-compliant and illegally imported devices, improve network performance and strengthen consumer confidence in devices sold in the country. It added that stolen devices reported through the appropriate channels could also be identified and blocked from operating across Nigerian mobile networks. The Commission has commenced the first phase of implementing the automated Type Approval compliance framework, working with the Nigeria Customs Service, Original Equipment Manufacturers, OEMs, importers and relevant market associations. The first phase is focused on onboarding existing devices currently held in stock and ensuring that devices imported into Nigeria going forward are appropriately registered and authenticated. NCC’s Director of Technical Standards and Network Integrity, Engr. Edoyemi Ogoh, said the Type Approval Business Rules issued in August 2024 provided the regulatory framework for establishing a Central Equipment Identity Register, CEIR, which maintains a registry of SIM-enabled communications devices in Nigeria. He said the central registry of IMEI numbers would enable the Commission to ensure that devices imported into, sold and used in Nigeria comply with applicable standards. “With the deployment of this system, all SIM-enabled communications devices brought into the country must be registered before they are sold. Devices that are not duly registered will not be permitted to operate on Nigerian networks,” Ogoh said. He added that the system would make it easier to identify illegally imported and non-compliant devices, while stolen devices could be blocked from use across Nigerian mobile networks. The NCC stressed that the DMS is therefore a regulatory and device-identification tool, rather than a platform for accessing or monitoring users’ personal communications. items.title: SSNIT honours 16 stakeholders at 2025 Awards
items.description: The Social Security and National Insurance Trust (SSNIT) has honoured 16 outstanding stakeholders for their commitment and contribution to the Social Security Scheme. The recognition took place at the 2025 SSNIT Stakeholder Awards, held last month at the La Palm Royal Beach Hotel in Accra. The awardees included employers, self-employed contributors, pensioners and partner organisations. Established in 2019, the SSNIT Stakeholder Awards Scheme recognises stakeholders whose compliance, consistency and partnership have contributed to the sustainability and growth of the Social Security Scheme. Speaking at the ceremony, the Deputy Director-General of SSNIT, in charge of Operations and Benefits, Mr. Adam Sulley, reaffirmed the Trust’s efforts to creating greater value for members through innovation and improved service delivery. “We remain committed to our members by making our services more accessible, responsive and convenient,” Mr. Sulley said. Deputy Director-General of SSNIT – Operations and Benefits – Adam Sulley He highlighted recent initiatives by the Trust, including the Virtual Branch, Membership Value Programme (MVP), Co-location with partner banks and the Telehealth Service, which are aimed at improving access to SSNIT services and enhancing the experience of members. He added that the Trust was strengthening its service-led approach and leveraging data to improve its operations and service delivery. The General Manager, Operations, Philip Kofi Senyah, described the awards as an opportunity to recognise stakeholders whose contributions continued to strengthen the Social Security Scheme. He stressed that the sustainability of the Scheme depended on the collective commitment and continued collaboration of all stakeholders. Awards Among the individual awardees, Snaider Konadu Owusu received the Youngest Ambassador Award, while Elvis Agyemeng was honoured with the Loyal Contributor Award. Fidelia Aku Amevuvor received the Distinguished Service Award, while Nem Robert Kweku was recognised with the Trailblazer Self-Employed Pensioner Award. The Lifetime Dedication Award was presented to Amadu Wala, the oldest living SSNIT pensioner, while the National Pensioners’ Association (NPA) received the Outstanding Growth Partner Award. In the establishment category, Zijin Golden Ridge Limited received the Ambassador of the Trust Award. The Diamond Compliance Award was presented to Burkina Chamber of Commerce Ghana Agency, Flexi-Space Ltd and Ernest Chemists Ltd in the small, medium and large establishment categories, respectively. Scanship Ghana Limited, Hull Blyth (Ghana) Limited and The Church of Pentecost received the Excellence in Contribution Award, while Rinacand Company Limited, Bishop Bowers School and SIC Insurance Company Ltd were honoured with the Legacy Partnership Award. Speaking on behalf of the award recipients, Rev. Sis Matilda Quist of Bishop Bowers School expressed appreciation to SSNIT for the recognition. She acknowledged the importance of the collective efforts of stakeholders in supporting and strengthening the Social Security Scheme. In her closing remarks, the Ag. items.title: Police arrest man over mother’s murder in Osun
items.description: By Shina Abubakar The Osun State Police command on Wednesday disclosed that it arrested one Taye Kasali for allegedly killing his mother, Mrs Kudirat Kasali over farm dispute. A statement issued by the command’s Public Relations Officer DSP Abiodun Ojelabi disclosed that the police in Bode-Osi in Ola-Oluwa local government received report that the deceased and her son were missing on September 1, 2026. Following the report, operatives from the command embarked on investigation and intelligence led to the arrest of the son, Taye, on September 7, 2026, and later confessed to killing his mother. The suspect led the police team to the farm where the body of his mother was recovered from a shallow grave along with the matchet used to slit the deceased’s throat before burying her. The statement disclosed that his mother had been referring to him as a mad person and threatening to lease out the farmland which the suspect claimed is the family’s source of income. Meanwhile, the Commissioner of Police Ibrahim Zungura has directed thorough investigation into the incident with view to charging him to court to face the wrath of he law. He also assured the residents of the State that Justice will be served in the case, urging the public to always report the cases of missing persons promptly to police as well s other criminal activities in their communities. The post Police arrest man over mother’s murder in Osun appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Obi: Ortom condemns blockade, says Alia is responsible
items.description: By Dickson Omobola Former Governor Samuel Ortom of Benue State has condemned the blockade of the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, Peter Obi, from visiting Yelwata community in Guma Local Government Area of the state, accusing Governor Hyacinth Alia of disrespecting the rule of law. Ortom said the incident was a reflection of the situation in Benue, noting that it was unfortunate that a clergyman who should be telling the truth was telling lies. Speaking on Politics Today, a Channels Television programme, Wednesday, Ortom alleged that Alia was behind the incident and challenged the governor to swear by the Bible that he was not aware of what happened. His words: “In Benue State, we have a government that does not believe in the rule of law. We have a government in Benue State that is out for lawlessness. We begin to wonder, if all of us will not respect the rule of law, but also join him in ensuring lawlessness, where are we going to be? This is a supposed man of God, a supposed priest of the Catholic Church. We know that even in the scriptures that we lean on, it says that we must respect the laws of the land. “But unfortunately, we have somebody who says he’s a Catholic priest and does not respect the rule of law in any way. I condemn what happened yesterday. It is wrong not to allow Peter Obi to visit Benue and sympathise with those people whose people were killed. It was wrong, and that is the kind of government that we have in Benue State today. “Governor Alia has been doing it. Governor Alia was one person who said, ‘No Alia, no Benue,’ and went to remove a Chief Judge through these thugs. Alia sent tippers with loads of sand to block the Chief Judge’s office. He has been saying that if nobody accepts him, he will not accept any other person. “I say that it is unfortunate that somebody who is supposed to be a reverend father is telling lies. Can he come out and swear by the Bible that he claims to be a reverend priest and say that he was not aware of what happened yesterday? It was a deliberate attempt. He did it. Ask any other person. “Alia himself, the governor of Benue State, is involved in this matter. He cannot deny that. I am not supporting Peter Obi. But it is wrong.” Meanwhile, former Governor of Bayelsa State and national leader of the NDC, Seriake Dickson, called for a thorough investigation and prosecution of those involved, saying Nigerians deserve to know the extent of complicity. Speaking on Newsnight, an Arise TV programme, Wednesday, he said there had been allegations that some government officials were involved in the incident and urged the authorities to establish whether the allegations were true. His words: “This happening, while campaigns have officially started, sends a very dangerous signal, and the point has to be made clearly that this is not only condemnable, it is criminal. This is rascality of the highest order, and this is intolerable. There has to be punishment for this, so that we can say, well, however bad things may have gone in this country, we can’t accept this to go on. Otherwise, we may have a situation where candidates will be attacked everywhere, or people will be encouraged wrongly to think or assume that a presidential candidate, or even any other candidate or any other Nigerian, needs a visa of some kind to be able to participate in any activity he or she wants to, or to visit any state. “No Nigerian citizen, by our Constitution and our laws, needs anyone’s permission or approval to visit a state. More so, when we are dealing with a presidential candidate, a high-profile personality, at a period of political campaigns, you stop the man with thugs. No, that is not encouraging. It sounds almost obscene. It tells where we have gone as a country, but we must speak against it. “We have just listened to the remarks that the Commissioner of Police made, even though we were all concerned about what steps the police took at that venue, or to prevent it. One of the first things I asked when it occurred, I called the national chairman and asked, was there notification to the state authorities? And they brought a copy of a letter, a letter by the state chairman to the Commissioner of Police. “Once you have informed the Commissioner of Police about the visit or activities of a politician or a high-profile personality, that is to be treated as information to the state authorities because the Commissioner of Police is the chief law enforcement officer of every state. “I’m pleased with the steps they have taken. I’m not surprised, but steps should have been taken to prevent it. By tomorrow, there will be a formal petition from our party to the Inspector-General and then to the Attorney-General of the Federation. And I think we have gotten to a point, before campaigns really kick off, for even the President of the country to weigh in on this. “He is sitting at the apex of the political system, and he’s not just President of the APC, he’s not just President of a particular set of people. He is the President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, and his job is not to talk about economic policies, which we disagree with. His job is not just political stability and security matters, which they are not doing well either. But part of the duties and responsibilities of the President in our system includes the preservation and protection of the democratic order and the democratic system.” The post Obi: Ortom condemns blockade, says Alia is responsible appeared first on Vanguard News .

Naa Shika Adu presents Vernacular of Play: An art exhibition inspired by sport, identity and social impact
items.description: Former women’s professional tennis player and internationally certified tennis coach Naa Shika Adu is set to launch Vernacular of Play on 11 September 2026, a compelling multidisciplinary art exhibition exploring the connections between movement, language and cultural expression in sport and everyday life. The exhibition is supported by the Edward Osei Boakye Trust and features a creative collaboration with artist Reginald Kofi Boateng, bringing together sport and visual art in a thought-provoking exploration of play, identity and culture. The exhibition reinterprets tennis as more than a competitive activity, positioning it as a powerful tool for social commentary. At its core, Vernacular of Play explores how movement transcends words, and how play serves as a compelling mirror of society, capturing its rhythms, inequalities, aspirations, and moments of collective joy. Central to this concept is the term “vernacular,” which historically carried negative connotations within colonial educational systems where indigenous speech and identity were often suppressed. In this context, the term is reclaimed and transformed into a symbol of cultural identity, memory and expression. Inspired by her experiences as both an athlete and a youth development advocate, Naa Shika creates an immersive space where art and sport intersect. Through a carefully assembled collection of works curated by Whitney Chinonye Ernest, the exhibition highlights themes of resilience, aspiration, discipline and community, while celebrating the universal significance of play. According to Naa Shika, “the body speaks long before words are formed. In Vernacular of Play, every movement, a serve, a sprint, a pause, or a moment of stillness becomes a sentence in a larger story, expressing emotions, struggles and triumphs that transcend language.” The exhibition further challenges the perception of sport as neutral. Tennis, often linked to privilege and exclusivity, is reframed through African perspectives and lived experiences. By combining performance, visual art, sound, archival storytelling and embodied movement, the project explores the deeper social meanings embedded within the choreography of play and how history is carried within the body, even in competitive spaces. Beyond its artistic intent, the exhibition also serves a broader social purpose. It supports the Africa Sports Alliance (ASA) Foundation, founded by Naa Shika, which is dedicated to using sport as a vehicle for youth empowerment across Africa. Through mentorship, structured programmes and access to opportunities, the Foundation seeks to develop talent, create employment pathways and equip young people with essential life skills. Vernacular of Play is therefore positioned as both a cultural and social engagement platform, bringing together artists, athletes, educators, corporate partners and the wider community in support of youth development. Its impact lies in its ability to connect sport, art and social consciousness in a way that is inclusive, participatory and culturally relevant. The exhibition creates opportunities for African youth to see themselves represented within contemporary narratives, while encouraging dialogue on issues such as access to sport, representation, postcolonial identity and cultural preservation. Ultimately, Vernacular of Play invites audiences to move beyond observation to active engagement, reflecting on how movement, language and play influence how societies remember the past, respond to the present and shape the future. It stands as a powerful testament to Naa Shika Adu’s commitment to driving meaningful change beyond the tennis court.

items.title: Camps de Tindouf : le Maroc appelle le HCR à financer des solutions durables
items.description: Devant le Comité permanent du HCR, le Maroc a dénoncé un système de financement des camps de Tindouf qui, depuis des décennies, entretient la crise au lieu de la résoudre, et appelé l'organisation à faire des « solutions durables » une priorité de sa planification budgétaire. Face à des besoins qui progressent et un budget qui impose des arbitrages douloureux, le Maroc a appelé, mercredi à Genève, le Haut-Commissariat des Nations unies pour les réfugiés (HCR) à inscrire les “solutions durables” dans sa planification budgétaire pour les camps de Tindouf, en Algérie, estimant que les financements consacrés depuis plusieurs décennies à cette situation reconduisent un “régime de maintien coûteux” plutôt qu’ils ne contribuent à la résoudre. Ces solutions durables consistent en le retour dans la dignité des populations concernées, conformément à l'appel solennel du Roi Mohammed VI, la réinstallation dans des pays tiers disposés à y contribuer et l'intégration dans le pays d'accueil, a indiqué l’ambassadeur représentant permanent du Maroc auprès de l’ONU et des autres organisations internationales à Genève, Omar Zniber, lors des travaux du Comité permanent du HCR. “Depuis 2021, près de 90 millions de dollars ont été mobilisés par le HCR dans les camps de Tindouf, en Algérie. Et dans le même temps, année après année, tout a régressé : le taux de malnutrition a doublé, l'autonomie économique s'est effacée, et l'accès à l’emploi demeure interdit – de sorte que la dépense a crû quand l'espérance, elle, a décru” , a-t-il relevé. Selon Omar Zniber, ces chiffres “ne décrivent pas un programme de protection” mais “un régime de maintien” , coûteux dans un contexte budgétaire contraint et insuffisant au regard des besoins des personnes concernées. A cet égard, l’ambassadeur a rappelé que le droit international des réfugiés prévoit “trois solutions durables” , à savoir “ le rapatriement librement consenti, la réinstallation et l’intégration dans le pays d’accueil ”, estimant que ce sont ces solutions qui permettent de mettre fin à la prolongation des dépenses liées aux situations de déplacement prolongé. Il a par ailleurs affirmé que le Royaume “assume pleinement sa part de cette responsabilité”, soulignant que cet engagement s'inscrit désormais dans “un cadre transformé: en adoptant la résolution 2797, le Conseil de sécurité a consacré l'initiative marocaine d’autonomie ouvrant un horizon politique là où ne subsistait qu'un statu quo”. A ce titre, “l'appel solennel du Roi Mohammed VI, au retour dans la dignité des populations concernées vaut engagement d'accueil, sans condition et sur une base strictement individuelle et volontaire” , a-t-il ajouté, notant que le Maroc “soutient également, avec la même conviction, les deux autres solutions – la réinstallation dans des pays tiers disposés à y contribuer et l'intégration dans le pays d'accueil – selon le choix libre de chaque personne”. Cette approche n'est pas isolée, a-t-il soutenu, expliquant qu’un nombre important d'États donateurs, parmi les premiers contributeurs au budget, se déclarent “prêts à financer ce qui résout plutôt que ce qui perdure”. Omar Zniber a, de ce fait, invité le HCR à “saisir cette disponibilité, en inscrivant les solutions durables au cœur de sa planification budgétaire et en engageant, avec les États concernés et les partenaires volontaires, l'examen des trois solutions avant la session du Comité exécutif”. “L’objectif de réduire de moitié les situations prolongées d’ici 2035 est d’abord un objectif budgétaire: il ne se décidera pas ailleurs qu'ici, dans l'affectation de chaque dollar ”, a-t-il conclu. The post Camps de Tindouf : le Maroc appelle le HCR à financer des solutions durables appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Ghana wastes up to 50% of fruits and vegetables annually – Agrofresh
items.description: Ghana wastes between 40% and 50% of its fruits and vegetables annually, social entrepreneur, innovator and changemaker Mathias Charles Yabe has said. He said the losses occur across the food value chain, from farms and marketplaces to homes, restaurants and food joints. Speaking on the 13th edition of the Loud and Green X-Space on JoyNews, Mr Yabe said the scale of food waste remained a major challenge requiring practical interventions. “Just in Ghana, we see at least about 40% of our food is being wasted in terms of fruits and vegetables being wasted every year. About 40 to 50%. So that is a current situation in Ghana,” he said. Mr Yabe said his interest in addressing post-harvest losses was influenced by experiences in farming communities, including a case where a farmer’s tomatoes were left to rot because buyers failed to arrive on time and there was no facility to store the produce. He said the challenge was particularly acute in farming communities without reliable access to electricity, where conventional refrigeration systems can be difficult to deploy. His company, Agrofresh, has consequently developed solar-powered refrigeration systems designed for farms and communities. “Basically, we are building fridges on farms and in communities. Essentially, these fridges are supposed to help preserve food and extend its shelf life, especially fruits and vegetables, from five days to up to 21 days,” he said. Mr Yabe said the refrigerators are powered by solar energy and are intended to serve communities that are off the national electricity grid. Agrofresh has also introduced solar-powered refrigerated tricycles to help reduce losses during the transportation of fresh produce. “We recently introduced solar-powered refrigerator tricycles. These tricycles are a complementary solution to the stationary and then the mobile refrigerated units,” he said. According to Mr Yabe, the intervention gives farmers another option for preserving their produce while it is being transported to markets. He said reducing post-harvest losses could simultaneously improve farmers’ incomes, strengthen food supply and reduce the environmental impact of food waste. The discussion formed part of the 13th edition of the Loud and Green X-Space, which examined opportunities emerging from Ghana’s climate challenges.

items.title: Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra vs iPhone Duo: Which foldable phone is better?
items.description: The Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra and Apple iPhone Duo are now competing for the attention of consumers looking for a premium foldable smartphone, with both devices offering large displays, powerful processors and high-end features. Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra and Apple’s first foldable iPhone, the iPhone Duo, take different approaches to the foldable phone experience. While Samsung has several years of experience making foldable smartphones, Apple is entering the market with a device designed to combine the iPhone experience with a larger, tablet-like display. Here’s how the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra compares with the iPhone Duo. Display The Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra has a larger 8-inch internal AMOLED display and a 6.5-inch cover screen. The iPhone Duo features a 7.6-inch internal OLED display and a smaller 5.4-inch external display. Samsung therefore has the advantage for users who want as much screen space as possible when the phone is unfolded. The larger display is particularly useful for browsing, watching videos, editing documents and running multiple applications simultaneously. Performance The Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra is powered by Qualcomm’s Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 for Galaxy processor. Apple’s iPhone Duo runs on the company’s latest A20 Pro chip. Both processors are designed for demanding applications, gaming and artificial intelligence features. However, direct performance comparisons will require independent benchmark and real-world testing before a clear winner can be declared. Camera Samsung has the more versatile camera setup. The Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra features a 200MP main camera, a 50MP ultrawide camera and a 10MP telephoto camera with 3x optical zoom. The iPhone Duo, meanwhile, uses two 48MP rear cameras. Although camera quality cannot be judged by megapixel counts alone, Samsung’s dedicated telephoto camera gives the Fold 8 Ultra an advantage for users who regularly photograph distant subjects. Apple, however, has a long-standing reputation for computational photography and video recording, meaning the iPhone Duo could still compete strongly despite having fewer cameras. Battery Samsung equips the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra with a 5,000mAh battery. Apple uses a dual-cell battery design in the iPhone Duo and has focused on delivering all-day battery life despite the phone’s thin foldable design. On paper, Samsung has the advantage in battery capacity, but actual battery performance will depend on factors including software optimisation, display usage and processor efficiency. Multitasking and productivity This is one area where the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra has a major advantage. Samsung has spent years developing its foldable software, allowing users to run multiple applications on the large internal display. The Fold 8 Ultra can effectively function as a small tablet when unfolded, making it particularly useful for people who work from their phones. Apple has also introduced software features designed specifically for the larger display of the iPhone Duo, but Samsung’s experience gives it an advantage in foldable multitasking. Durability The Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra has an IP48 rating. The iPhone Duo has a higher IP68 rating, giving Apple’s device an advantage in water and dust resistance. Durability remains an important consideration for foldable phones because their flexible displays and hinges are more complicated than those found on conventional smartphones. Price The Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra starts at around $2,100, while Apple’s iPhone Duo starts at $1,999. That makes Apple’s first foldable iPhone slightly cheaper at launch. However, prices in markets such as Nigeria can differ considerably from US launch prices because of taxes, import costs, exchange rates and retailer margins. Which one should you buy? The Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra is the stronger choice for users who prioritise productivity, multitasking, camera versatility and a large internal display. Samsung’s experience in the foldable market also means buyers are getting a more mature foldable platform. The iPhone Duo, on the other hand, is likely to appeal most to existing Apple users who want a foldable phone without leaving the iOS ecosystem. For users with a MacBook, Apple Watch, AirPods and other Apple devices, the iPhone Duo offers the convenience of keeping everything within Apple’s ecosystem. All the Places Trump Was on 9/11
items.description: Updated at 4:30 p.m. ET on September 9, 2026 W here were you on 9/11? Every American old enough to remember the day has an answer to that question. President Trump has several. At a ceremony honoring first responders and victims’ families yesterday, Trump offered an elaborate account of where he was in the hours and days after nearly 3,000 Americans were killed. “I was building a big building in New York, and I took the whole crew down there right after this happened, and they had no hesitation; everybody went down with me. We went down as a big group of people. Wasn’t too much we could do, I’ll be honest. It was raw—nobody had seen anything like it, ever.” The story presents significant problems in terms of its relationship to reality. Listeners could be forgiven for interpreting Trump’s remarks as a reference to his whereabouts on the day of the attack itself. (The president clarified that timeline last night: “I was there, obviously not on the same day as the collapse, but shortly thereafter, with a large group of Construction Workers,” he wrote in a Truth Social post.) It is true that two days after the attack, on September 13, Trump was interviewed by reporters while walking in Lower Manhattan. The president has previously made variations of the same claim—that he and the employees he sent downtown helped clear rubble in the days following the attack. “Everyone who helped clear the rubble—and I was there, and I watched, and I helped a little bit” was his version of it on the 2016 campaign trail. But supporting evidence is scant, and the whole account is likely an exaggeration. Richard Alles, a retired New York City Fire Department deputy chief who had a supervisory role in the efforts, said in 2019 not only that he never witnessed Trump at the site, but that the account doesn’t add up: “He was a private citizen at the time. I don’t know what kind of role he could have possibly played.” And, Alles added , if Trump had indeed sent workers, as he has claimed, there would be a record of it: “Is there a chance he was ever down there by himself and I didn’t know it? It’s possible, but I know of no one who ever witnessed him there.” Nevertheless, Trump pressed on, veering into territory even further detached from verifiable fact. The U.S. Steel Building—a skyscraper in Lower Manhattan known today as One Liberty Plaza—was “really creaking,” Trump said at yesterday’s ceremony. “I’ll never forget: two firemen. We thought it was coming down on top of us and two firemen—big, strong guys. And I’m not the smallest guy in the world. They grabbed me under the arms, said, ‘Gotta get outta here.’ And they literally lifted me up—this is not easy to do; I’m big. They lifted me up, and they started running with me. I said, ‘Fellas, I can run myself.’ But they were amazing, but they thought it was coming down. It didn’t come down: U.S. Steel.” There was, in fact, public concern in the days following the attack that the building at One Liberty Plaza could collapse. But the notion that Trump was inside the building and rushed out by firefighters has not been corroborated by any evidence. The president has offered versions of the same account before, though in less colorful form. In 2016, he told a story about being evacuated by firefighters—but in that rendition, it took place “a couple of days” after the collapse, and the U.S. Steel building was “not so far from us” when the two “massive guys” grabbed him. “I never knew I could run that fast,” he said then. In 2021, Trump likewise recalled two firemen grabbing him after hearing “creaks.” Trump’s whereabouts on September 11 are no mystery. They are fairly well documented by his own prior statements about watching the attacks unfold from his home in Trump Tower, about four miles north of the Twin Towers. For those who have reason to doubt Trump’s statements, his whereabouts are also documented on video. “I have a window that looks directly at the World Trade Center, and I saw this huge explosion,” he said in a phone interview with a New Jersey news channel on 9/11. “For years, I’ve looked right directly at the building—I’d see the Empire State Building in the foreground and the World Trade Center in the background—and now I’m looking at absolutely nothing. It’s just gone, and it’s just hard to believe.” Trump’s view may have been clear, but his recollection of September 11 has been murky, as reporters have tracked for more than a decade. Sometimes, in his accounts, he watched the second plane hit the World Trade Center from his apartment in Trump Tower; when he called into the live broadcast that day, he did not mention having witnessed the second jet. Sometimes, he claims to have personally seen people jumping from the Twin Towers. “I have a window in my apartment that specifically was aimed at the World Trade Center,” he said in 2015 on the campaign trail, “and I watched as people jumped.” In his TV interview the day of the attack, he didn’t see those scenes himself but talked to someone who had. “I have somebody that was down there who witnessed at least 10 people jumping out of the building from 70 and 80 stories up in the air,” Trump said. The president has also embellished what he saw in news coverage on that day, most notoriously claiming to have seen widespread celebrations by Muslim residents in New Jersey. “I watched when the World Trade Center came tumbling down,” he said in a 2015 stump speech. “And I watched in Jersey City, New Jersey, where thousands and thousands of people were cheering as that building was coming down.” That claim has been thoroughly disproved. A professor who spent months combing through news reels and video archives from that day found one possible instance that could slightly resemble those events—a few Arab American teenagers who briefly gathered in front of a library in South Paterson in a way that could be seen as celebratory. Even the live phone interview Trump participated in on the day of the attack contains inaccuracies. On the call, Trump said that one of his buildings was now the tallest in downtown Manhattan: “Forty Wall Street actually was the second-tallest building in downtown Manhattan,” he said when asked whether his property had been damaged. “When they built the World Trade Center, it became known as the second tallest. And now it’s the tallest.” But as The Washington Post documented , using data from the Council on Tall Buildings and Urban Habitat, neither claim was true. Forty Wall Street was the tallest building for only about two years and that was in the 1930s, before Trump was born. A t the center of yesterday’s ceremony was an important honor—one that Trump had promised to bestow months prior. Welles Crowther, who was first identified as “the man in the red bandana” in a 2002 New York Times story, rescued more than a dozen people from the South Tower before being killed when the building collapsed. His parents, who had given him a red bandana as a boy and knew that he always carried it with him, were able to recognize him by that detail and confirmed through the survivors that their son had helped them. Crowther was an equities trader and a volunteer firefighter, and he was 24 years old when he died. While awarding a posthumous Presidential Medal of Freedom to Crowther, Trump drew the focus to himself, comparing his own fame to that of the fallen hero: “The Man in the Red Bandana, he’s become more famous than me—I don’t like it. Very unhappy. But he’s become much more famous than me.” [ Read: Trump is putting his face on everything ] When the president has brought up 9/11 lately, the remark has usually been severed from the attack, its victims, or its perpetrators. This year, Trump has tended to mention the day in the context of lambasting political opponents. He’s invoked it on several recent occasions—alongside World War I, World War II, and Pearl Harbor—when arguing that the attack and all three of those historical calamities are dwarfed by the danger communism poses to America today. Critics have noted that other presidents, both Republican and Democrat, might have faced months of blowback—if not the end of their political careers—were they caught exaggerating or outright inventing aspects of their experience on one of the most catastrophic days in American history. But Trump has rarely if ever paid a real political price for misleading statements. In a second term marked by his fixation on his legacy, Trump’s relationship with history has often involved “taking bits and pieces from a grab bag and turning it into a story that’s useful to him—either politically useful, as in the case of his fabrication about Muslims celebrating 9/11, or making himself the center of a story that obviously he was not the center of 25 years ago,” Tim Naftali, a presidential historian at Columbia’s School of International and Public Affairs, told me. The fabrications are unlikely to stop, he said, especially as the president ages . “It doesn’t happen the same to all men in their 80s, but we may see more of this: new recollections about the past that we’ve never heard before, because they never happened,” Naftali said. The White House did not address my specific questions about the president’s most recent claims, but Davis Ingle, a White House spokesperson, said in a statement that the president “was relaying his experience of a city reeling” from the attacks. September 11 continues to be a point of tension about what the government owed, and continues to owe, those who were most affected. The mayor’s office released more than 170,000 pages of city records this week showing that city officials misled New Yorkers about air quality following the attacks. And the health toll continues to grow; the number of 9/11 survivors receiving assistance for cancer treatment roughly tripled over the past five years, according to a Washington Post analysis of reports by the World Trade Center Health Program, which funds health care for responders and survivors. Twenty-five years later, Americans everywhere will pause to remember what the nation lost that day—both those who suffered directly and those who lived through it by watching the tragedy unfold from the safety of their homes, much as Trump did. This article originally stated that Welles Crowther was posthumously awarded the Presidential Medal of Honor. In fact, he was awarded the Presidential Medal of Freedom.

items.title: Village gastronomique de Paris : ce qui vous attend au pavillon Algérie
items.description: Parmi les 73 pays qui vont participer à la 10e édition du Village international de la gastronomie de Paris, du 10 au 13 septembre, figure l’Algérie, qui s’est taillé une part du lion concernant le nombre des stands. Cet évènement international verra la participation de chefs cuisiniers venus des quatre coins du monde, dont Na Nora, qui va préparer sa célèbre galette farcie et un couscous spécial. Les Algériens ne seront pas en reste, et tenteront de hisser le drapeau national au plus haut, grâce notamment à la richesse de sa cuisine et à l’authenticité de ses produits de terroir. La nouvelle édition de cet événement sera donc lancée demain, jeudi 10 septembre. Le Village international de la gastronomie s’installera Place de la Concorde, à deux pas des Champs-Elysées. Les visiteurs auront donc l’occasion de déguster des préparations culinaires en tout genre, notamment algériennes, pas loin de la Tour Eiffel. Village gastronomique de Paris : le pavillon algérien s’élargit Lors de cet évènement, l’Algérie aura droit à deux stands, de 9 m² chacun, en ce qui concerne la gastronomie, et quatre autres stands pour ce qui est des produits du terroir, a dévoilé Makhlouf Chalal, organisateur du stand Algérie, à VVA , samedi dernier. L’Algérie figure ainsi parmi les rares pays qui bénéficient d’autant de stands lors de cet évènement culinaire international. L’organisateur algérien souligne que le pavillon DZ a doublé d’espace “après le succès de l’année passée . Ce nombre de stands peut facilement s'expliquer par la richesse et la diversité de la cuisine algérienne, qui propose, entre autres, couscous, rechta, chakhchoukha, kesra, bourek. Les produits de terroir algériens sont aussi légion. On cite notamment l'huile d'olive de Kabylie, les dattes Deglet Nour, les figues sèches de Béni Maouche, ou encore les divers produits laitiers traditionnels. Pavillon algérien : plusieurs activités au menu Contacté par TSA, M. Chalal a indiqué que le pavillon DZ proposera aussi plusieurs activités, notamment un défilé de tenues traditionnelles (Kaftan, Karakou, Blouza, Robe kabyle, Chedda, etc) le 12 septembre à 10h et un spectacle assuré par une troupe folklorique, le 11 septembre à 19h. Pour ce qui est de la gastronomie, plusieurs chefs algériens seront au rendez-vous. Na Nora (Nora Sadki), la célèbre cheffe du restaurant Majouja à Paris, participera à l'événement. “Au sein du Pavillon algérien, j’aurais le plaisir de vous accueillir pour 4 jours de célébration de notre patrimoine culinaire et de tous les plats qui nous rassemblent”, a-t-elle écrit, soulignant qu’il s’agit d’une occasion “de mettre en lumière les artisans, les chefs et les producteurs locaux”. Na Nora va préparer la galette farcie ou la pizza kabyle que les visiteurs pourront déguster. « Il y aura aussi une surprise vendredi avec le couscous algérien », annonce la cheffe algérienne à TSA. « Du couscous avec du kedid (viande séchée) », précise-t-elle. Une première au Village gastronomique de Paris. La cuisine algérienne est si riche et son terroir si généreux. Les six stands qui représenteront en tout l’Algérie au sein de ce village promettent de faire découvrir aux visiteurs des délices inoubliables et un savoir-faire millénaire. L’article Village gastronomique de Paris : ce qui vous attend au pavillon Algérie est apparu en premier sur TSA .
