items.title: CSSPS deploys more personnel to ease delays at resolution centres
items.description: The Computerised School Selection and Placement System (CSSPS) has deployed additional personnel to some resolution centres across the country following concerns over long queues and delays in addressing parents’ placement challenges. Speaking on Joy FM’s Newsnight , the Media Relations Officer at the Ministry of Education, Hashmin Mohammed, said the move was prompted by reports of some centres struggling to attend to the large number of parents seeking assistance. “We have been notified of the delays and then the long queues across some of the resolution centres in the country, and accordingly the coordinator for the CSSPS, with the support of some of the ministry officials, have decided to deploy more personnel into the areas that are unable to attend to the complainants with speed of time,” he said. Mr Mohammed said the placement authorities had also established a decentralised system to make it easier for parents to have their concerns addressed. He explained that the resolution centres operate a 24-hour service, with parents issued tickets that enable them to track the progress of their complaints. He, however, acknowledged that the challenges would persist unless the gap between available vacancies and students’ preferred schools is addressed. “The problem that exists at the moment is just the disparity between where vacancies exist and then the mismatch between the choices of the students, and that is what we are currently dealing at the moment,” he said. According to him, thousands of parents have so far had their concerns addressed, although he could not provide an immediate figure. Mr Mohammed also cautioned parents against paying money to individuals to fast-track their placement concerns. He said allegations of some persons demanding money at resolution centres had been brought to the attention of officials in the Ashanti Region, who have been asked to take steps to prevent such practices. He stressed that parents are not required to pay any official or third party for CSSPS placement services.

items.title: Obi Attack: SERAP urges Tinubu to direct IGP to take over case
items.description: The Socio-Economic Rights and Accountability Project (SERAP) has condemned the reported attack on Peter Obi, presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), and his entourage in Benue State. In a statement on Wednesday signed by Kolawole Oluwadare, SERAP Deputy Director, it urged President Bola Tinubu to “direct the Inspector-General of Police, IGP Olatunji Rilwan Disu to take over the investigation into the incident, ensure a prompt, thorough, impartial, transparent and effective investigation, and identify anyone responsible for the attack and anyone who sponsored, facilitated or otherwise aided it, with a view to prosecution where there is sufficient admissible evidence.” Obi was reportedly visiting Benue State on Tuesday when suspected thugs confronted and stopped his convoy along Gboko Road in Makurdi, near the Air Force Base. The incident reportedly occurred shortly after the convoy arrived in the state. The Benue State Police Command has confirmed the incident and commenced an investigation. The organisation said: “the IGP should take over the case to ensure that the investigation is conducted independently and comprehensively, including determining whether any public officials, political actors or other persons were involved in, sponsored, facilitated or condoned the reported attack.” SERAP said: “The reported attack is a serious threat to political participation, civic space and Nigeria’s democratic process. It is an affront to the 1999 Constitution (as amended) and Nigeria’s international human rights obligations, including under the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights and the African Charter on Human and Peoples’ Rights, to which Nigeria is a state party.” According to SERAP, “The authorities must ensure that politicians, candidates, journalists, civil society actors and other citizens are able to freely exercise their rights to freedom of expression, peaceful assembly, association, and political participation without fear of intimidation or attack.” The statement, read, in part: “SERAP is seriously concerned that attacks, threats and intimidation against political actors undermine constitutionally and internationally guaranteed human rights and risk further shrinking Nigeria’s already fragile civic and political space, particularly as the country moves towards the 2027 general elections.” “The reported incident must also be viewed against Nigeria’s troubling history of political violence, intimidation and impunity.” “The failure to investigate and prosecute political violence would deny victims justice and create an atmosphere of impunity that emboldens further attacks.” “Allowing attacks and intimidation against political opponents to go unpunished would undermine the rule of law and public confidence in Nigeria’s democratic institutions.” “No individual or political group should be above the law. Impunity for political violence can only embolden further attacks and threaten the integrity of Nigeria’s democratic process.” “SERAP urges all political parties, candidates, supporters and public officials to refrain from threats, inflammatory rhetoric and violence and to respect the rights of political opponents and citizens to participate freely in public affairs.” “The Nigerian Constitution guarantees rights freedom of expression, peaceful assembly and association. Article 13 of the African Charter on Human and Peoples’ Rights and Article 25 of the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights guarantee the right of every citizen to participate freely in the government of their country.” “These rights would be meaningless if political actors and citizens could not exercise them without fear of threats, intimidation or violence.” “Nigeria cannot afford a repetition of the cycle of political violence and impunity that has undermined previous elections. President Tinubu must act swiftly to direct the Inspector General of Police to establish the facts, identify anyone responsible and their sponsors, hold them accountable and protect political participants ahead of the 2027 general elections.” “Accountability for the reported attack is essential not only to secure justice but also to send a clear message that political violence and intimidation will not be tolerated.” The post Obi Attack: SERAP urges Tinubu to direct IGP to take over case appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Programme Génération AI & IoT : six mois après son lancement, le programme national passe à l’échelle
items.description: S’inscrivant dans la dynamique impulsée par les Hautes Orientations du Roi Mohammed VI, qui placent la jeunesse, le développement de ses compétences et son accès aux opportunités d’avenir au cœur des priorités du Royaume, le programme national Génération AIoT franchit une nouvelle étape de son déploiement. Cette initiative s’inscrit pleinement dans les ambitions de Maroc Digital 2030 et contribue à la mise en œuvre de la feuille de route « AI Made in Morocco », en misant sur le développement des compétences nationales dans les technologies de l’intelligence artificielle et de l’Internet des objets, au service de l’innovation, de l’emploi et de la souveraineté numérique du Royaume. Fruit d’un partenariat stratégique entre le Ministère de la Transition numérique et de la Réforme de l’Administration, la Fondation Mohammed V pour la Solidarité et ABA Technology, Génération AIoT ambitionne de préparer une nouvelle génération de talents marocains aux technologies qui façonnent l’économie de demain, notamment l’Intelligence Artificielle, l’Agentic AI, le Physical AI et l’IoT, en associant formation et mise en application sur des projets concrets. À l’occasion de sa visite du centre de Salé, Madame Amal El Fallah Serghouchni, Ministre déléguée auprès du Chef du Gouvernement chargée de la Transition numérique et de la Réforme de l’Administration, a constaté les premiers résultats du programme, six mois seulement après son lancement. Signé et lancé en février 2026, Génération AIoT a déjà enregistré plus de 2 118 candidatures et compte 95 talents à Salé et Casablanca. À Salé, la première promotion de 46 talents a achevé en quatre mois son cursus de formation et de spécialisation avant de passer, dès le 24 juin, aux projets en environnement professionnel. 100 % des talents entrés en phase d’immersion sont aujourd’hui intégrés à des projets appliqués, couvrant notamment la santé, les mines et l’industrie, la finance et la logistique, la recherche scientifique, l’éducation et les technologies numériques. Fort de ces premiers résultats, le programme entre désormais dans sa phase de montée en puissance nationale, avec l’ouverture de nouvelles promotions à Casablanca, Fès et Oujda, en complément de Salé. Avec 3 promotions à Casablanca, 2 à Fès et 2 à Oujda, Génération AIoT vise un régime de croisière de 1 200 talents formés par an dès février 2027. En moins d’un an, Génération AIoT entend ainsi passer du lancement à une capacité nationale de 1 200 talents par an, avec une ambition : faire de la jeunesse marocaine un acteur de la transformation technologique et productive du Royaume. The post Programme Génération AI & IoT : six mois après son lancement, le programme national passe à l’échelle appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Clôture du PASS III : le Maroc et l’UE préparent l’après-réforme sanitaire
items.description: À Rabat, la cérémonie de clôture du Programme d’appui au secteur de la santé (PASS III) a été l’occasion pour le Maroc et l’Union européenne de dresser le bilan de six années de coopération, tout en esquissant les contours d’un partenariat renouvelé autour de la souveraineté sanitaire, de la transformation numérique et du renforcement des ressources humaines. La clôture du Programme d’appui au secteur de la santé (PASS III), organisée mercredi 9 septembre à Rabat, a marqué bien davantage que la fin d’un cycle de coopération entre le Maroc et l’Union européenne. Elle a surtout servi de tribune aux deux partenaires pour affirmer leur volonté de prolonger et d’approfondir une collaboration engagée depuis plus de deux décennies dans le domaine de la santé. Signé en 2020, le PASS III a accompagné le Royaume dans plusieurs chantiers structurants : renforcement des capacités de veille et de réponse aux crises sanitaires, amélioration de la gouvernance du système de santé, développement des soins de santé primaires, démarches d’accréditation hospitalière ou encore préparation de la nouvelle gouvernance territoriale du secteur. Présent à la cérémonie, le ministre de la santé et de la protection sociale, Amine Tehraoui, a salué un programme qui « a accompagné le Maroc dans le renforcement de ses capacités de veille, de préparation et de réponse aux crises sanitaires », tout en contribuant à la modernisation de l’offre de soins et à la préparation des réformes en cours. Le ministre a également rappelé le soutien apporté par l’Union européenne à la reconstruction et à la mise à niveau des établissements de santé touchés par le séisme d’Al Haouz, soulignant que ces réalisations constituent des « acquis importants » pour le système sanitaire national. Une coopération bâtie sur les réformes Pour l’ambassadeur de l’Union européenne au Maroc, Dimiter Tzantchev, le PASS III illustre la profondeur d’une relation qui dépasse le simple cadre de l’assistance technique ou financière. « Ce programme n’est pas seulement un appui technique ou financier. Il est l’illustration d’une ambition partagée : accompagner les réformes du système de santé marocain dans une approche structurante, durable et centrée sur les besoins de la population », a-t-il déclaré. Selon le diplomate européen, les résultats du programme se mesurent autant à travers les outils de pilotage développés qu’à travers le renforcement des capacités institutionnelles et techniques des acteurs du secteur. Il a notamment mis en avant les actions de formation, les dispositifs d’accréditation hospitalière, les mécanismes de suivi ainsi que les expérimentations territoriales destinées à préparer les évolutions futures du système de santé. Dimiter Tzantchev a insisté sur le fait que « la transformation d’un système de santé ne repose pas uniquement sur des investissements matériels », mais aussi sur « des réformes de gouvernance, des outils fiables, des compétences renforcées, des mécanismes de coordination efficaces et une vision de long terme ». La santé, nouveau pilier du partenariat euro-méditerranéen Au-delà du bilan, les deux parties ont surtout mis l’accent sur les perspectives d’avenir. Pour l’ambassadeur européen, la santé est devenue un enjeu stratégique dans un contexte marqué par les transitions sanitaires, démographiques, numériques et climatiques. « Investir dans la santé, c’est investir dans la dignité humaine, dans la cohésion sociale, dans la réduction des inégalités et dans la stabilité de nos sociétés », a-t-il affirmé. Cette vision s’inscrit, selon lui, dans le cadre du nouveau Pacte pour la Méditerranée, qui place davantage les citoyens au cœur de la coopération entre les deux rives. Le ministre de la santé a, de son côté, estimé que la clôture du PASS III devait être considérée comme « le début d’une nouvelle étape de notre coopération avec l’Union européenne », alors que le Maroc poursuit la mise en œuvre de la réforme de son système de santé et du chantier de généralisation de la protection sociale. « Notre ambition est claire : construire un système plus équitable, plus performant et plus résilient », a-t-il déclaré, jugeant que cette transformation exige à la fois des investissements conséquents et des partenariats durables. Numérisation, souveraineté sanitaire et ressources humaines Les interventions des deux responsables ont convergé autour de plusieurs axes appelés à structurer la coopération future. La transformation numérique figure parmi les priorités identifiées. Amine Tehraoui a souligné l’importance de la gouvernance et de la valorisation des données de santé, devenues « des enjeux majeurs de performance, de qualité et de souveraineté ». Une orientation partagée par l’Union européenne, qui voit dans les systèmes d’information interopérables, la télémédecine et l’intelligence artificielle des leviers d’amélioration des soins et de réduction des inégalités territoriales. Autre chantier commun : la souveraineté pharmaceutique et vaccinale. Le ministre a rappelé que le Maroc dispose désormais d’une base industrielle solide et entend renforcer les partenariats favorisant l’innovation, la production locale et l’accès équitable aux produits de santé. L’Union européenne s’est dite prête à accompagner cette dynamique, notamment à travers le partage d’expertise, le renforcement des capacités réglementaires et le développement de partenariats industriels. Les deux parties ont également mis l’accent sur la sécurité sanitaire et la préparation aux crises futures. La pandémie de Covid-19 a montré, selon Dimiter Tzantchev, que les systèmes de santé sont interdépendants et que la coopération en matière de surveillance épidémiologique, de recherche et de gestion des risques doit être renforcée. Enfin, la question des ressources humaines apparaît comme un défi commun. « Sans femmes et hommes bien formés, reconnus et soutenus, aucune réforme ne peut réussir durablement », a rappelé l’ambassadeur européen. Une analyse partagée par le ministre, qui a plaidé pour un effort accru en matière de formation, de développement des compétences et de mobilité des professionnels de santé. Au terme de cette cérémonie, le PASS III apparaît ainsi comme une étape de transition. Si le programme s’achève officiellement, Rabat et Bruxelles ont clairement affiché leur intention de faire de la santé l’un des piliers du nouveau partenariat stratégique approfondi entre le Maroc et l’Union européenne, dans une logique davantage tournée vers l’innovation, la résilience et la souveraineté sanitaire. items.title: 2027: SDP ‘ll alleviate poverty, transform Nigeria’s future – Adebayo
items.description: Social Democratic Party (SDP) presidential candidate, Prince Adewole Adebayo, says the party will rescue Nigeria from poverty and insecurity. Adebayo ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‌‍‍‍⁠‌​‍​‌​stated this at the party’s September National Convention, entitled: “Consolidating the blueprint for a new Nigeria to secure our homeland and defeat poverty”, on Wednesday in Abuja. He maintained that Nigeria’s immense natural resources were divinely provided to guarantee prosperity for the country. On the SDP core mission, Adebayo emphasised the party stood apart from other political platforms because its members were driven by collective nation-building rather than personal self-glorification. He drew a historical parallel with the aborted 1993 presidential election widely believed to have been won by the late Chief MKO. Abiola, noting that the poverty the party fought to defeat decades ago had since grown and consumed citizens. ​”The poverty that SDP fought with Nigerians’ mandate to defeat and eradicate in 1993, that poverty has grown up and has consumed babies,” he stated, stressing the urgent need for a unified national rescue mission. Addressing the country’s current economic struggles, the presidential candidate argued that Nigeria’s under-development was not a result of a scarcity of natural wealth, but a failure of visionary governance. According to him, Nigeria possesses enough oil, gas and other mineral deposits to rival and surpass major global economies. ​”If God wanted us to be poor, he would not deposit under us sufficient minerals that no civilisation in human history had got before,” Adebayo asserted. He outlined a grassroots strategy focused on door-to-door mobilisation to win the hearts and minds of every day citizens. The presidential candidate urged party members to reject politics driven by personal enrichment and instead, focus on uniting the country ahead of the upcoming elections. ​”Our intention is known to God, and it’s simply that we will get Nigerians to accept that we don’t desire to be poor, and we don’t desire to die of insecurity. Everything we need to succeed is already here,” he said. The Vice-Presidential candidate of the party, Prof. Usman Bugaje, reinforced the party’s reformist stance. Bugaje warned that the country might face critical threats if citizens continued to value transactional ‘big man’ politics over genuine structural change. He noted that the party’s framework required individuals who were committed to national transformation rather than financial gains or superficial party size metrics. ​”People should be here not because they want money; people should be here because they want this ten-page change,” Bugaje stated, challenging the conventional Nigerian political obsession with labelling parties as “big” or “small.” He called for absolute integrity, sacrifice and ideological clarity among party faithful to steer the country away from its current challenges. items.title: Poor transport and storage systems contribute to post-harvest losses in Ghana – Mathias Yabe
items.description: The absence of appropriate transportation and storage systems is contributing to post-harvest losses among farmers, particularly those dealing with highly perishable crops, social entrepreneur and innovator Mathias Charles Yabe has said. Speaking on the 13th edition of the Loud and Green X-Space on JoyNews, Mr Yabe said the transportation of fresh produce could result in significant losses before the food reached consumers. He cited the experience of a lettuce farmer near the Dodowa Road who supplies produce to a buyer in Spintex. According to him, the farmer previously transported the lettuce by Aboboya to a lorry station before continuing the journey by trotro. He said the produce could break and wilt during the journey, significantly reducing the farmer’s earnings. “If the farmer is expecting to make GH¢1,500, by the time she gets to the buyer, she may end up with about GH¢700,” he said. Mr Yabe, however, said the losses should not simply be blamed on the farmer but should be viewed as evidence of the need for better systems to move perishable produce from farms to markets. As part of efforts to address the challenge, Agrofresh introduced a solar-powered refrigerated tricycle. “We recently introduced solar-powered refrigerated tricycles. These tricycles are a complementary solution to the stationary and then the mobile refrigerated units,” he said. Mr Yabe said the tricycle was piloted in collaboration with the Netherlands Embassy, Holland Green Tech and Eden Tree. He said one of the farmers who participated in the pilot reported no losses while using the refrigerated tricycle to deliver produce. “The farmer reported zero losses when she used our tricycle for the delivery,” he said. The intervention forms part of Agrofresh’s broader efforts to reduce post-harvest losses through solar-powered refrigeration. Mr Yabe said the company also builds refrigeration units that can be installed on farms and in communities to preserve fresh produce for longer periods. “Basically, we are building fridges on farms and in communities. Essentially, these fridges are supposed to help preserve food and extend its shelf life, especially fruits and vegetables, from five days to up to 21 days,” he said. He said the initiative was particularly relevant to farming communities where limited access to electricity made conventional refrigeration difficult to deploy. The discussion, which examined opportunities emerging from Ghana’s climate challenges, formed part of the 13th edition of the Loud and Green X-Space.

items.title: 24 die, many hospitalised after consuming herbal drinks in Ondo
items.description: By Dayo Johnson Akure Twenty-four persons have reportedly died while others were hospitalised in Araromi Obu and Odigbo towns in Odigbo Council Area of Ondo State, following suspected food poisoning. The incident, which occurred last weekend, has triggered anger in the affected communities. Youths took to the streets to protest the deaths and marched to the palace of the traditional ruler of Araromi Obu, Oba Rufus Akinrinmade, demanding urgent action to prevent further loss of lives. Eight deaths were recorded in Araromi Obu, while 16 were recorded in Odigbo town. Sources said the fatalities may be linked to the consumption of poisonous substances suspected to be contained in sachet herbal concoctions. Some of the deceased reportedly died in their homes, while others died in their sleep. Addressing the protesters, the traditional ruler of the community, Oba Akinrinmade, appealed for calm and assured them that efforts would be made to ascertain the circumstances surrounding the deaths and provide a lasting solution. The Permanent Secretary, Ondo State Ministry of Health, Dr. Ayodele Adiji, said preliminary findings suggested a possible link between the deaths and the consumption of locally brewed alcoholic beverages. Adiji specifically mentioned a locally produced drink as well as other herbal and ethanol-based drinks. He added that laboratory analysis of samples collected was ongoing to establish a direct connection. In response, the Chairman of Odigbo Local Government, Hon. Taiwo Adegoroye, imposed a one-month ban on the sale and consumption of locally brewed herbal drinks in the area as a precautionary measure. Adegoroye said a preliminary verbal autopsy by the council’s health team indicated a possible link between the deaths and the substances. He warned that anyone found selling or distributing the banned drinks during the restriction period would face arrest and prosecution. The State Commissioner for Health, Dr. Banji Ajaka, said investigations were underway to determine the actual cause of the deaths. Ajaka added that government was taking the matter seriously and would provide further details after assessments in the affected communities. Health authorities have urged residents to avoid consuming suspicious herbal concoctions or unverified sachet products pending the outcome of investigations. The Police spokesperson in the state, DSP Jimoh Abayomi, said that the command in collaboration with the government and relevant health authorities, have commenced a comprehensive investigation into the incidents with a view to determining the actual cause of the reported deaths. Abayomi noted that ” police personnel including Police Medical Services are working closely with officials of the Ondo State Ministry of Health and the Odigbo Local Government health authorities in the collection of relevant information and evidence, while medical and toxicological examinations are being conducted to ascertain the substance, if any, responsible for the fatalities. He cautioned “members of the public against spreading unverified information or attributing the deaths to any particular substance, as the investigation and laboratory analyses are still ongoing. “The actual number of casualties and the precise cause of the deaths will be established through the ongoing investigation. Abayomi advised “residents of the affected communities to remain calm and cooperate with the authorities by providing useful information that may assist the investigation. ” Members of the public are also urged to refrain from consuming unregulated or suspicious alcoholic and herbal preparations pending the outcome of the investigation. He said that “the Command is committed to unraveling the circumstances surrounding the unfortunate incidents and will take appropriate action against anyone found culpable. “The Command will continue to liaise with the Ondo State Government and relevant agencies and will provide further updates as soon as credible findings emerge. items.title: NELFUND has provided financial relief to less privileged – Shettima
items.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru The Vice President, Senator Kashim Shettima, has described the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND) established by the administration of President Bola Tinubu as a landmark initiative that has provided crucial financial relief to the children of the poor and removed the financial barriers to higher education. The administration, according to him, positioned the Fund as a vital social equalizer and a primary mechanism for poverty alleviation as well the advancement of education in Nigeria. Senator Shettima stated this on Wednesday in Abuja during an audience with the management team of the University of Abuja, led by the Vice Chancellor, Prof. Hakeem Babatunde Fawehinmi. The Vice President said that by ensuring tuition fees are covered and providing monthly upkeep allowances, the scheme—which targets students from less-privileged backgrounds who would otherwise be excluded from tertiary education—has ensured that poverty is no longer an excuse not to go to school. Recalling his days as student at the University of Maiduguri when the price of food surged at the cafeteria, he said the “NELFUND is a very beautiful initiative by the leadership of this country under President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, created to give respite breathing space to the children of the poor.” VP Shettima also observed that Nigeria has crossed the rubicon and is firmly on the path of sustainable economic development under the Tinubu administration. He cited the recent upgrade of Nigeria’s sovereign credit ratings and outlooks by global rating agencies, attributing the success to stronger foreign exchange reserves, higher oil production, increased federal allocation following the removal of oil subsidy, and the ongoing macroeconomic reforms undertaken by the Renewed Hope administration. He applauded the management of the University of Abuja under the leadership of Prof. Fawehinmi, saying the Vice Chancellor has provided leadership that has surmounted the challenges that confronted the school in the past. The University of Abuja, he observed, is now standing on a solid pedestal, as real stability has been restored in the institution, even as he pledged that the federal government will do everything within its ability to give the school the needed support. Earlier, the Vice Chancellor of the University of Abuja, Prof. Fawehinmi commended Vice President Shettima for supporting and spearheading the growth and developmental strides of the Tinubu administration. The Vice Chancellor described VP Shettima as a mentor whose leadership qualities have assisted the University’s Governing Board to manage the school, even as he sought the institution’s partnership with the government to move the country forward. “We have always known you to be a highly cerebral and dynamic leader. We appreciate the generous strides you are making in the country. We are not surprised at your intellectual agility,” he stated. Prof. Fewehinmi said NELFUND, under the Renewed Hope Agenda of President Tinubu, has assisted immensely in bringing relative stability in the nation’s education sector, pointing out that students are able to go to school and are able to sustain their stay in the school.” He stated that the management as well as the Governing Council of the University of Abuja deemed it necessary to thank the Vice President for the support he has always given to the school. “Our recent history in terms of leadership has not been very palatable. There have been issues to do with our checkered history, but in the last eight months when we came on board, we tried our very best to stabilize the university,” he explained. items.title: Partisan MMDCE elections could stifle development – NDC
items.description: The National Democratic Congress (NDC) has defended government’s position against fully partisan elections for Metropolitan, Municipal and District Chief Executives (MMDCEs), arguing that such an arrangement could undermine development at the local level. Deputy Director of Elections and Information Technology of the NDC, Rashid Tanko Computer, said Ghana’s political culture makes it risky to have MMDCEs from a political party different from the party controlling central government. Speaking on Joy FM Top Story on Wednesday, September 9, he cited the possibility of an opposition MMDCE being elected in major cities such as Kumasi or Accra while a different political party controls central government. “Imagine you have His Excellency John Dramani Mahama and the NDC government in place, and then you are going to have an NPP man being an MCE in Kumasi or Accra. What do you expect? What kind of correlation are you going to have? It’s going to stifle development,” he stated. According to him, Ghana’s system of local governance must take into account the country’s political culture and traditions rather than simply adopting governance models from Western countries. “We can’t just go and borrow the democracy practices in the Western world and come and implement it in totality. We will have difficulties in implementing major decisions and other things, because you know the politics we do in Ghana,” he said. Mr Tanko Computer further defended government’s proposed model for selecting MMDCEs, insisting it would still give residents a meaningful opportunity to choose their local leaders. Under the proposed arrangement, five candidates would first be selected and subjected to interviews by the Public Services Commission. Three candidates would then proceed to the final stage, where residents within the district would vote to select their MMDCE. He said the proposed system is significantly different from the current arrangement, under which the President nominates an individual and assembly members vote on the nominee. “This one government has no role in it. And then they will now go and have universal suffrage within the district of which they are going to preside over, and they will decide their seat over there. It’s not the assemblymen who will now decide the seat. So it’s completely different,” he said. Mr Tanko Computer maintained that the proposed system seeks to balance democratic participation with the need for effective coordination between local and central government. His defence follows the Trades Union Congress (TUC) rejecting government’s proposal for the selection of MMDCEs, insisting that districts must be allowed to independently choose their leaders.

items.title: TUC urges Mahama to keep constitutional reform discussions open
items.description: The Trades Union Congress (TUC) is urging President John Mahama to keep discussions on the proposed constitutional reforms open to allow for broader consultation and consensus-building. Deputy Secretary-General of the TUC, Dr Kwabena Nyarko Otoo, said the union intends to engage the President and members of the constitutional reform implementation committee to further present its views on some of the recommendations. Speaking on Joy FM Top Story on Wednesday, September 9, Dr Otoo said the union also intends to engage the chairperson and members of the constitutional reform implementation committee to persuade them to reconsider some of the proposals. “We continue to appeal to the government not to foreclose the discussions. There are still more people with varying opinions, and it is important that we hear everything, everybody,” he said. He said the ultimate goal should be to build broad consensus around a reformed Constitution that strengthens Ghana’s democracy and contributes to the country’s economic and social transformation. Dr Nyarko Otoo also said the TUC disagrees with concerns that allowing the election of mayors along partisan political lines could threaten Ghana’s unity. He argued that several African countries, including Nigeria, Kenya and Senegal, elect local government leaders through partisan political processes without undermining their national cohesion. “The fear that electing a mayor for Kumasi or Ho, who is different, with a different political persuasion from the governing party, will break up the country, is an unfounded fear.” According to Dr Otoo, Ghana’s democratic development should extend to the grassroots, particularly in local governance. He maintained that partisan local elections could provide an opportunity to deepen democracy and improve the effectiveness of local governance. “We need to have absolute democracy at all levels,” he said. Dr Otoo said the TUC will continue to dialogue with government on the matter and plans to formally write to President Mahama to seek an audience.

items.title: Comoé : Deux adolescents meurent par noyade dans une retenue d’eau à Niangoloko
items.description: BURKINA-COMOE-NOYADE-ADOLESCENTS Comoé : Deux adolescents meurent par noyade dans une retenue d'eau à Niangoloko Niangoloko, 9 sept. 2026 (AIB)-Deux adolescents, âgés de 14 et 17 ans et issus d'une même famille, ont trouvé la mort par noyade, mardi soir, dans une retenue d'eau de Niangoloko, alors qu'ils étaient partis y pêcher. Selon des témoignages recueillis sur place, les deux frères étaient en train de pêcher lorsque le plus jeune est accidentellement tombé dans l'eau. En tentant de lui porter secours, son grand frère s'est à son tour retrouvé en difficulté. Malgré ses efforts, il n'a pas pu sauver son cadet, et les deux adolescents ont péri par noyade. Alertée, la Brigade nationale de sapeurs-pompiers (BNSP) de Banfora est intervenue pour repêcher les corps des victimes. Après les constatations d'usage effectuées par le commissariat de police de district (CPD) de Niangoloko, les dépouilles ont été remises à la famille pour inhumation. En cette période de saison des pluies, la BNSP appelle les parents à sensibiliser davantage leurs enfants sur les dangers liés aux cours et retenues d'eau. Elle invite également la population à faire preuve de la plus grande prudence aux abords des points d'eau. Agence d'information du Burkina BBH/no/ata

items.title: Does Trump Want Republicans to Win the Midterms?
items.description: Is Donald Trump trying to help Republicans win the midterm elections? The obvious answer to this question is yes, of course , simply because all political leaders benefit from their party winning elections. Yet several of Trump’s actions throw this normally perfunctory question into at least some doubt. Traditionally, candidates laboring under the burden of an unpopular president seek to detach themselves from the national brand. Trump is making this impossible. He has launched a national ad campaign focused on himself, and thrown a high-profile “midterm convention” designed to further reinforce the synonymity of the party and its leader. Trump has also made several remarks that convey an emotional detachment from the election’s outcome—comments such as “I’m not affected by the election” or “I don’t care about the midterms.” Perhaps he is merely feigning indifference. Maybe he truly does not care. More likely, Trump cares about the outcome, but not enough to permit Republicans to acknowledge his lack of popularity. His approach, at any rate, nicely illustrates the drawbacks of handing total control of a political party to an egomaniac. Midterm elections have historically disfavored the president’s party. Candidates for office who are running in neutral or hostile territory accordingly tend to emphasize their differences with the president—think of Joe Manchin running an ad in West Virginia in 2010 showing him firing an actual bullet at Barack Obama’s cap-and-trade bill, or the Republican Will Hurd in 2018 criticizing Trump’s racism and affinity for Russia. [ Listen: Trump’s economy goes to the polls ] Trump’s public standing is unusually dire. He is currently polling far worse than either he did at this point in 2018 or Joe Biden did four years ago. In theory, this ought to give Republicans an especially strong incentive to edge away from Trump and emphasize local themes in their elections. Trump has decided to block this escape route. He is commandeering earned media with his “Trumpapalooza” show, drawing attention to the person endangered Republicans desperately need their constituents to forget. He has hoarded the party’s ad budget, warning Republicans, “This is my money that I control,” and that he would spend it on “Republicans that I think are good,” which is to say, slavishly loyal. He has promised to barnstorm the country, telling reporters, “I’ll be making a lot of stops,” including in Alaska, where the Republican Dan Sullivan is trailing. There is an old Simpsons episode in which the elderly oligarch Montgomery Burns informs the obsequious Smithers that, upon his own death, his loyal aide will be buried alive at his boss’s feet. Trump appears to be thinking along similar lines. This self-defeating behavior makes a degree of sense if you accept that Trump’s interest in politics is purely egocentric. He has difficulty caring about anything that does not directly involve himself, and the prospect of Republicans holding seats by repudiating his record is likely unpalatable. The benefits of same-party control of Congress are also smaller for Trump than other presidents, because he governs mainly through executive action. To the extent that a Democratic majority in either chamber might threaten him with oversight, he will surely disregard it, as he did during his first term. Although he finds Republican majorities preferable, the size of those majorities matters to him far less than their composition—a fully loyal minority may seem preferable to a fractious majority. What makes less sense is the willingness of many Republicans to cooperate with a strategy that consigns many of them to defeat. Consider, for instance, Mike Rogers, the Republican Senate candidate in Michigan. Rogers came up through politics long before Trump entered it, and is trying to win office in a state where the president’s approval rating is 25 points underwater. A recent poll of the state found Trump’s endorsement made voters less likely, by a 55 percent to 27 percent margin, to support a candidate. Yet Rogers has opened no daylight whatsoever with the unpopular president, even echoing his false claims of having the 2020 election stolen from him. When Trump launched a trade war with Canada, a move that poses an especially dire threat to Rogers’s own state, he declined to take the opportunity to display independence. Instead, he issued a statement mumbling his approval. (“President Trump is right to put America First—and tariffs are necessary, but are not a one-size-fits-all solution . ”) The same dynamic is occurring in other races, where Trump is throwing himself behind incumbents who are in danger mainly because voters don’t like him. [ Read: Trump plans to buy midterm ads about his own record ] To be sure, some Republicans subscribe to the theory that the Trump era has suspended normal midterm election dynamics. According to this account, a decisive sliver of voters are loyal to Trump, and not his party. Republicans can win only by enticing them to vote, which means making the election about their hero. “We’ve seen that a lot of Trump voters—they will crawl over glass to vote for the president,” one Republican strategist explained to Politico . Yet Trump has tried before to insert himself into non-presidential elections. And his efforts have mostly failed—not only in the 2018 midterms, when he refused to lie low, but also in multiple off-schedule elections (the most famous case being Georgia’s 2021 Senate runoff, which he made into a referendum on his effort to overturn the 2020 election). In the Trump era, his party has fared well only when it has been able to focus on the shortcomings of unpopular Democratic opponents, such as Hillary Clinton in 2016 and Biden and Kamala Harris in 2024. Making elections about Trump—which also occurred when he ran for reelection in 2020—has been a losing gambit. The political tip sheets in recent days have been filled with the lamentations of fatalistic Republican operatives. “We have no choice. We’re stuck on the boat with him whether we like it or not,” a top Republican campaign official confessed to Axios . They cannot stop Trump from staging Trumpapalooza, so they are reduced to praying for low ratings. “My only hope is that no one watches it since it’s competing versus NFL opening games,” a person close to the White House told Politico . “Hopefully nobody notices the embarrassing show.” Republicans are cooperating in a strategy that sacrifices their best chance of political survival, because the past decade has trained them to believe that resistance to Trump is futile. Trump did far less damage to the country during his first term, both because institutions and norm-following officials restrained him, and because his pathological instincts frequently undermined his support. The former limitation has broken down in the second term, but the latter one remains. Trump’s support has collapsed in large part because of his own poor choices.

items.title: Khadim Mboup, le « Génie en herbe » est devenu grand
items.description: En 2014, devant la présentatrice de l’émission Oumy Ndour, il avait donné une réponse avant même que la question ne fût achevée. Valdiodio Ndiaye. Vingt points. Une fulgurance qui avait fait de Khadim Mboup l’un des visages les plus familiers du tournoi national de « Génies en herbe ». Douze ans ont passé. Le jeune prodige de Louga a grandi, étudié à Lyon, Lausanne et au Québec. Les mathématiques ont rencontré l’économie. Et derrière les diplômes, une conviction s’est précisée : le Sénégal ne manque pas de cerveaux, il lui manque encore les moyens de les faire éclore, de les retenir, de les mettre au service de son propre destin. En 2014, sur la scène de la finale nationale de « Génies en herbe », Khadim Mboup livrait un récital de culture générale dont le souvenir n’a pas disparu. Mais derrière le champion que le petit écran avait révélé, il y avait un garçon que l’école avait patiemment façonné. En 2026, Khadim ne répond plus à la manière du garçon de 2014. Il regarde plus loin. « Ce qui me revient immédiatement, ce n'est pas tant la finale elle-même que ce qui s'est passé après », dit-il. Après, plusieurs élèves venaient lui demander comment devenir « cultivés », comment travailler, comment progresser. C’est cette image qui lui est restée. Pas le trophée. Pas les caméras : « Ça m'a fait réaliser que cette compétition n'avait pas seulement une valeur pour moi ou pour mon lycée. Elle inspirait ». Né à Genève, Khadim est profondément façonné par Louga où il grandit. L’enfant fréquente l’école coranique avant de rejoindre l’école sénégalaise. Cette première formation, il en parle encore. « C'est un ensemble de choses qui se sont conjuguées : mes parents, l'environnement familial, une curiosité qui était sans doute déjà là en moi, mais surtout l'éducation que m'a donnée ma grand-mère et mon passage à l'école coranique », explique-t-il. Pourtant, Khadim n’a pas suivi une route scolaire parfaitement rectiligne. Il a dû rattraper trois années, sauter des classes pour se mettre à niveau. En classe de quatrième, on décide de le présenter au Bfem comme candidat libre. Il termine premier de son centre d’examen. « Je pense que c'est là que quelque chose a basculé en moi », se souvient-il. Après, tout s’enchaîne. La série S. Les mathématiques. Le Concours général sénégalais où il obtient une distinction. Puis « Génies en herbe », remporté en 2014 avec le lycée Malick Sall. Le baccalauréat S1 avec mention. Des réussites qui pourraient donner l’illusion d’une trajectoire sans heurts. Lui-même récuse cette lecture trop simpliste. « Il n'y a pas eu un déclic isolé, séparé du reste. C'est venu naturellement, comme un prolongement de tout ce qui m'avait construit jusque-là », explique-t-il. Il comprend que ses études peuvent le conduire bien au-delà des frontières du Sénégal. Alors il part. Lyon d’abord, à l’Université Claude Bernard, pour des études scientifiques. Puis Lausanne, en Suisse, pour les mathématiques. Enfin le Québec, à l’Université Laval, où les mathématiques se frottent à l’économie. Une géographie universitaire qui aurait pu éloigner le jeune Lougatois de ses premières attaches. « Ce que j'ai ressenti surtout, c'est le besoin de rester moi-même », raconte-t-il. Il arrive dans des environnements universitaires exigeants sans se présenter en élève venu de loin qu’il faudrait d’abord rassurer. Il vient pour apprendre. Découvrir. Comprendre. S’imprégner. « Je suis resté sénégalais, avec cette même soif de savoir qui m'animait depuis l'école coranique et Génies en herbe », confie-t-il. Patriotisme Depuis l’étranger, Khadim Mboup mesure davantage l’étendue du potentiel sénégalais. Il voit les talents. Les capacités d’innovation. La jeunesse. Il voit aussi les lenteurs, les insuffisances, les occasions manquées. Il parle de formation scientifique, de réformes, de la place de la science, de la manière d’enseigner. Il parle aussi de la décolonisation de l’éducation, de la façon dont le savoir est transmis, des connaissances que l’on choisit de valoriser. Ce n’est plus le candidat de « Génies en herbe » qui parle. C’est un jeune scientifique devenu économiste, un Sénégalais qui a vu d’autres systèmes universitaires et qui revient par la pensée vers celui qui l’a formé. Il ne dit pas que tout est à refaire. Il dit que beaucoup reste à faire. Le Sénégal, estime le champion, ne propose pas encore suffisamment d’offres de formation scientifique de haut niveau. Mais le problème va plus loin. Même des diplômés issus d’écoles d’excellence sénégalaises, comme l’École Polytechnique de Thiès ou l’École nationale de la statistique et de l’analyse économique (Ensae), finissent par partir après leur formation. Khadim y voit une contradiction : « On investit dans la formation de ces jeunes, mais on ne construit pas les conditions pour les retenir ni les mécanismes pour les intégrer directement au service du pays. » Son interrogation est concrète. Pourquoi les diplômés de l’École nationale d’administration (Ena) bénéficient-ils d’une prise en charge par l’État et d’un parcours professionnel dans la fonction publique alors que les diplômés des filières scientifiques et techniques ne disposent pas du même cadre ? La question n’est pas théorique. Elle concerne ceux qui devront demain bâtir les infrastructures, produire les statistiques, concevoir les modèles économiques, penser les politiques publiques. « Ce sont pourtant ces profils, ingénieurs, statisticiens, économistes, mathématiciens, dont le Sénégal a le plus besoin pour bâtir ses infrastructures, penser ses politiques publiques avec rigueur et accélérer sa transformation économique », affirme-t-il. Il faut donc, selon lui, cesser de faire du retour au pays une simple affaire de volonté individuelle. Le jeune diplômé parti à l’étranger n’est pas nécessairement quelqu’un qui tourne le dos à son pays. Il peut être quelqu’un qui cherche les conditions de son propre accomplissement. Il y a son engagement, oui. Son désir de mettre ses compétences en mathématiques et en économie au service du développement du Sénégal. Mais il y a aussi la responsabilité de l’État de créer les conditions qui rendront ce choix possible. « Tant que cette cohérence n'existe pas, on continuera à demander à des jeunes de revenir sacrifier des opportunités, sans leur offrir en retour un cadre à la hauteur de leur formation », avertit-il. Entre-temps, les mathématiques ont changé de place dans son esprit. Elles ne sont plus seulement la discipline dans laquelle il excellait. Elles sont devenues un outil. Lorsqu’il se tourne vers l’économie à l’Université Laval, Khadim ne tourne pas le dos aux nombres. Il les emmène avec lui. « Je ne vois pas ce passage comme un abandon des mathématiques, mais comme un prolongement naturel », précise-t-il. Soif d’apprendre et de comprendre Le garçon qui cherchait les réponses aux questions de culture générale s’intéresse désormais aux mécanismes qui façonnent la vie des sociétés. Et lorsqu’il regarde le Khadim de 2014, il ne renie rien. « Ce qui n'a jamais changé, c'est l'essentiel : cette soif d'apprendre et de comprendre, cette rigueur héritée de l'école coranique, et cette spiritualité qui m'accompagne partout où je vais », dit-il. Il est resté Sénégalais. Resté talibé. Resté curieux. Resté calme. Mais quelque chose a changé dans son regard. Élève, il apprenait pour réussir. Pour aller plus loin dans ses études. Aujourd’hui, le savoir porte une autre charge. Cette même soif de savoir s'est transformée en une volonté de comprendre les grands enjeux du Sénégal et de l'Afrique, et surtout en une envie de servir, de mettre tout ce parcours au profit de son pays. Voilà le chemin parcouru. Le reste est encore à écrire. Khadim Mboup ne parle pas de son avenir en termes de carrière personnelle. Il parle de transformation. D’un Sénégal capable de compter sur ses propres forces, de construire une économie endogène et souveraine, de donner à ses jeunes les moyens de leurs rêves. À ses yeux, le pays regorge de talents, de jeunes brillants, mais qu'il manque encore les structures pour les révéler, les former et les retenir. « Je veux m'engager concrètement auprès de la jeunesse sénégalaise, essayer humblement de montrer, à travers mon propre parcours imparfait, qu'il est possible de viser l'excellence sans jamais renier ses racines », lance Khadim. Par Adama NDIAYE

items.title: Bougouriba/Bondigui : autorités et populations mobilisées contre les gîtes larvaires
items.description: Bougouriba/Bondigui : autorités et populations mobilisées contre les gîtes larvaires Bondigui, 8 septembre 2026 (AIB)- Les autorités locales et les populations de la commune de Bondigui se sont mobilisées, samedi 5 et dimanche 6 septembre 2026, dans le cadre de la deuxième phase des Journées nationales de lutte anti-vectorielle (JN-LAV), consacrée à la réduction des gîtes larvaires et à la prévention du paludisme. L’activité a mobilisé les services d’hygiène et d’assainissement de la mairie, le personnel de santé, les Forces de défense et de sécurité (FDS), des commerçants, des jeunes ainsi que des leaders religieux. Après une première phase marquée par une forte adhésion des populations, cette deuxième étape a notamment permis de constater et de vérifier la mise en œuvre effective des actions d’assainissement engagées dans la commune. Les équipes déployées sur le terrain ont parcouru plusieurs artères de Bondigui à la recherche de potentiels gîtes larvaires. Elles ont procédé à leur destruction et sensibilisé les populations sur les bonnes pratiques d’assainissement. Des pneus usagés, susceptibles de retenir les eaux de pluie et de favoriser la prolifération des moustiques, ont notamment été collectés et détruits le long de certaines voies. Les opérations ont également porté sur les caniveaux, dont l’entretien et le curage contribuent à limiter la stagnation des eaux et, partant, la formation de gîtes larvaires. L’infirmier chef de poste (ICP) du Centre de santé et de promotion sociale (CSPS) de Bondigui, Salia Dao, a rappelé que le paludisme demeure l’une des principales causes de morbidité et de mortalité au Burkina Faso. Selon lui, la période hivernale constitue une période particulièrement favorable à la multiplication des gîtes larvaires, d’où la nécessité de renforcer les actions préventives au sein des communautés. Dans les domiciles, les équipes ont également sensibilisé les ménages sur l’importance de maintenir leur environnement propre et de supprimer tout objet ou récipient susceptible de retenir de l’eau. Les populations ont notamment été invitées à se débarrasser des jarres, bidons, pneus et autres ustensiles abandonnés. Des démonstrations pratiques de destruction des gîtes larvaires ont été réalisées afin de permettre aux habitants de mieux maîtriser les gestes simples à adopter au quotidien pour limiter la prolifération des moustiques vecteurs du paludisme. Pour les acteurs de la lutte anti-vectorielle, l’implication des communautés constitue un maillon essentiel dans la réduction durable du paludisme et dans l’atteinte de l’objectif national d’élimination de la maladie à l’horizon 2030. Le responsable du service d’hygiène et d’assainissement de la mairie de Bondigui, Domondiele Pascal Hien, a exhorté les populations à maintenir leur cadre de vie propre. « Rendre propre son cadre de vie, c’est se protéger et protéger son entourage contre le paludisme », a-t-il déclaré, invitant les habitants à faire de la lutte contre les gîtes larvaires une pratique quotidienne. Il a également appelé les populations à s’approprier durablement les Journées nationales de lutte anti-vectorielle afin de faire de l’assainissement un réflexe collectif dans la commune. Agence d'Information du Burkina HDP/kmg/ata

items.title: Diphtheria: No outbreak in Lagos – Abayomi
items.description: By Chioma Obinna The Lagos state Commissioner for Health, Prof Akin Abayomi on Wednesday raised its disease surveillance and preparedness against diphtheria, warning residents not to panic but to remain vigilant as the outbreak continues to spread in parts of Nigeria. Abayomi, however, said there is currently no outbreak of diphtheria in Lagos, despite recording 53 suspected cases in 2026, six of which were laboratory-confirmed. The Commissioner, who gave the assurance at a media briefing on the state’s diphtheria preparedness and response, said the government was taking precautionary measures because of the high level of movement between Lagos and states currently battling the disease. According to him, the situation requires vigilance because Lagos’ huge population and extensive connections with other parts of the country could facilitate community transmission if imported cases are not detected and managed early. “We are appealing to all Lagosians to remain calm. There is no current outbreak of diphtheria in Lagos. We are simply taking precautionary measures,” Abayomi said. The Commissioner said the government was particularly concerned about the outbreak reported in states including Kano, Katsina, Kaduna, Benue and Zamfara, noting that the continuous movement of people between Lagos and affected areas made surveillance imperative. “We are watching this outbreak expand, and we are cautious in Lagos, as always. The Executive Council always likes to err on the side of caution and increase our prevention strategies in the state,” he said. Abayomi explained that diphtheria is a serious bacterial respiratory infection capable of causing life-threatening complications when treatment is delayed. He said the disease could produce a toxin capable of attacking the heart, while swelling and a thick membrane in the throat could obstruct breathing and swallowing. “There are two major things that happen to a patient with diphtheria. First, it can block the breathing apparatus in the throat, preventing the person from breathing normally or swallowing liquids and food properly. “Secondly, the toxin can enter the blood and travel to the heart, causing problems with the heartbeat and, eventually, heart failure.” He warned that an undiagnosed infection could therefore progress rapidly into airway obstruction and inflammation of the heart. Abayomi urged anyone developing severe sore throat, fever, weakness, neck swelling, difficulty breathing or swallowing, particularly after travelling to an affected state or having contact with a confirmed case, to seek medical attention immediately. “If you have any of these symptoms, present yourself quickly to one of our primary healthcare centres or your doctor so that we can make the diagnosis, carry out the necessary diagnostic workup and start treatment as quickly as possible,” he said. Giving an update on the situation in Lagos, Abayomi disclosed that 53 suspected diphtheria cases had been recorded in the state so far in 2026. Only six, he said, were confirmed through laboratory diagnosis, with all six cases appropriately managed. He added that contacts of confirmed patients were traced and placed under observation throughout the incubation period to detect possible secondary infections. “In Lagos, we have had sporadic cases of diphtheria. In fact, in 2026, we have had 53 suspected cases. Of those 53, only six have been confirmed through laboratory diagnosis,” he said. The Commissioner stressed that early diagnosis significantly improves the chances of successful treatment. “The treatment for diphtheria is very effective if the disease is diagnosed early,” Abayomi said, explaining that treatment involves antibiotics and medication capable of neutralising the toxin produced by the bacteria. While stressing that immunisation remains the most effective protection against diphtheria, Abayomi disclosed that only about 64 per cent of children in Lagos have received full vaccination coverage. He urged parents and guardians to check their children’s immunisation records and ensure that they receive all three doses of the pentavalent vaccine. “If you have received three doses, then you have significant protection. If you have received two, one or none, then you are vulnerable,” he warned. According to him, the three doses are expected to be administered at six, 10 and 14 weeks. He said Lagos has more than 1,000 healthcare facilities providing routine immunisation services across the public and private sectors, with vaccines available free at government facilities. The Commissioner clarified that primary healthcare centres are mainly vaccination points and are not the facilities designated to diagnose and manage suspected diphtheria cases. He listed the four designated centres as the Infectious Disease Hospital, Yaba; Massey Street Children’s Hospital, Lagos Island; Lagos University Teaching Hospital, LUTH; and Lagos State University Teaching Hospital, LASUTH. “If we suspect a case of diphtheria, we refer the patient to designated facilities. These are the four centres where we actively manage suspected cases of diphtheria. They have the capacity to make the diagnosis and manage the complications,” Abayomi said. He noted that severe cases could require advanced intervention to maintain the patient’s airway and close monitoring of the heart to prevent fatal complications. With schools expected to reopen soon, Abayomi said the Ministry of Health was working with the education sector to strengthen awareness and vaccination among schoolchildren. He said suspected cases in schools would trigger contact tracing and other infection-control measures. The Commissioner also urged residents to observe basic respiratory hygiene, including covering the mouth and nose when coughing or sneezing, washing hands regularly and avoiding close contact with others when experiencing respiratory symptoms. Speaking, the Permanent Secretary, Lagos State Ministry of Health, Dr. Dayo Lajide, also appealed to parents to ensure their children are fully vaccinated. “More importantly, we have to make sure that all our children are vaccinated,” Lajide said. She also urged the media to play a responsible role by providing accurate information to prevent unnecessary panic while encouraging residents to take appropriate preventive measures. She added that the government’s heightened surveillance was not a declaration of an outbreak in Lagos, but a precautionary response designed to ensure that any suspected case is detected, isolated, investigated and treated before it can trigger wider transmission. The post Diphtheria: No outbreak in Lagos – Abayomi appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: “They showed up with character” – Sampson praises Black Princesses after South Korea win
items.description: Black Princesses head coach Charles Sampson has praised his players for showing character and determination in their 3-1 victory over South Korea at the 2026 FIFA U-20 Women’s World Cup. Ghana bounced back from a disappointing 3-1 defeat to Ecuador in their opening Group C game to secure a crucial victory over the South Koreans on Wednesday. Sampson was impressed with the response from his players, saying they demonstrated the character, belief and passion needed to turn their fortunes around. “Today, the team actually really showed up. They showed up with the character that we know they have in the team. They believe in themselves and each other,” the Black Princesses coach told GFA Media. “And today, they exhibited it exactly how it should be, with a lot of enthusiasm and passion. They made up their mind that we’re gonna take this day, and that’s what happened.” The victory moves Ghana up to second place in Group C and keeps their hopes of progressing to the next stage of the tournament alive. The Black Princesses will now turn their attention to their final group game against France.

items.title: Ligue des champions: le FC Barcelone s'amuse face à Feyenoord
items.description: A l'image de ses débuts tonitruants en championnat d'Espagne, le FC Barcelone a parfaitement lancé sa Ligue des champions en surclassant le Feyenoord Rotterdam (5-1), grâce notamment à un doublé de Raphinha, mercredi au Camp Nou. Les Barcelonais, leaders de la Liga grâce à leur carton plein (4 victoires) et un total impressionnant de 17 buts, ont affiché la même efficacité offensive en C1 face aux Néerlandais. Il n'a fallu que trois minutes au capitaine blaugrana Raphinha pour ouvrir la marque. Trouvé par Lamine Yamal, l'actuel meilleur buteur de Liga (6 buts) a devancé un défenseur, puis en a éliminé deux autres grâce à une feinte du gauche, avant de loger une frappe au fond des filets. C'est ensuite l'une des recrues estivales du Barça, Karim Adeyemi, qui a assuré le spectacle en doublant la mise d'une superbe frappe enroulée du droit (22e). Après la pause, Raphinha, décidément inarrêtable en ce début de saison, s'est offert un doublé après un service parfait de Pedri (57e). Le champion du monde espagnol Lamine Yamal a corsé l'addition d'un magnifique coup franc (77e), avant d'offrir le cinquième but à la recrue Gabriel Jesus, buteur de la tête (85e). Feyenoord avait réduit le score par Sem Steijn (82e). Lors de la prochaine journée (13 octobre), le Barça se déplacera à Istanbul pour affronter Galatasaray avant d'aller se mesurer une semaine plus tard au Paris SG, double tenant du titre. items.title: Goods transport owners demand release of containers seized by Islamabad police
items.description: ISLAMABAD: Goods transporters on Wednesday demanded that the Ministry of Interior release containers detained by Islamabad police ahead of the PTI’s scheduled Islamabad long march at the end of the month. The PTI, with the confidence and support of the opposition alliance — Tehreek-i-Tahaffuz Ayeen-i-Pakistan (TTAP) — has announced a long march towards Islamabad against what it calls the “illegal” detention of party founder and ex-premier Imran Khan and to demand his release. The Islamabad High Court (IHC) on Tuesday decided to form a larger bench to hear a petition against the PTI’s planned protest, terming the matter sensitive and observing that it could have constitutional implications. In a statement on Wednesday, All Pakistan Goods Transport Owners Association President Muhammad Owais Chaudhry expressed concern over the seizure of container vehicles by Islamabad police, saying that the vehicles and containers should not be used for political purposes or to block roads during possible political activity on September 27. He said that around 100 container vehicles had been taken into custody from different areas of Islamabad, mainly Sangjani and Tarnol, the statement said. “The containers were being kept to possibly to block roads during the anticipated protest.” “What we demand is that there are a large number of containers available for rent in and around the federal capital — the Islamabad police or the administration should rent empty containers and use them as they wish,” Chaudhry was quoted as saying. He added that some impounded vehicles had reportedly been parked in deserted areas, while containers had allegedly been removed from certain vehicles, causing financial losses and business difficulties for their owners. “We had to facilitate the transporters in removing the goods from the containers — because the authorities do not take responsibility for the loss or damage to the cargo,” he added. Meanwhile, the association said it had received complaints from transporters alleging that some seized vehicles and containers were released after money was paid, while several others remained in police custody. It demanded a transparent investigation into the allegations and said the transporters had political affiliations on an individual basis. Their opposition to the impounding of vehicles, it added, should not be construed as a political link with the PTI, as the commercial vehicles were meant for trade and economic activity, “not for safety and security purposes of the police department”. The association also warned the government against impounding the vehicles, saying their forced use for political purposes created “an impression of state coercion”.

items.title: Free tablets , missed opportunities ? Rethinking Ghana’s one student-one tablet initiative
items.description: Ghana’s digital education investment needs digital discipline to succeed. Ghana’s Free Senior High School (Free SHS) programme has significantly expanded access to secondary education. As the programme evolves, the government has complemented it with a major digital education intervention, which is the One Student–One Tablet initiative, announced in January, 2023 and formally launched on 25th March, 2024 under the Ghana Smart Schools Project. The initiative was designed to provide SHS and TVET students with tablets containing educational resources to support research, teaching and learning. The vision is undoubtedly commendable. But as a teacher and school counsellor, I believe we must now ask a more fundamental question: Are students using these tablets for the purpose for which they were provided? From my everyday interaction with students, it appears that although some use the devices productively, many spend considerable time on gaming, entertainment, social interaction, watching videos and other activities unrelated to their studies. This presents a paradox: we have successfully placed technology in the hands of students, but have we done enough to prepare them to use it responsibly? The problem is not the tablet. The tablet initiative is a brilliant intervention. Properly used, a single device can serve as an electronic library, research centre, classroom and repository of textbooks, past questions and other learning materials. The challenge is, therefore, not access to technology but digital behaviour. A student may pick up the tablet intending to research an academic topic and, within minutes, become distracted by entertainment, games or social media. Consequently, providing a device does not automatically produce better learning. Digital access must be accompanied by digital discipline. Students need digital literacy and self-regulation Adolescents require guidance in managing technology responsibly. Students must learn how to distinguish educational use from social use, manage screen time, evaluate online information, protect their privacy and maintain appropriate digital behaviour. This means that the One Student–One Tablet initiative should be viewed not merely as a technology programme but also as an educational, behavioural and counselling intervention. Schools should deliberately incorporate digital citizenship, responsible social media use, internet safety, time management, cyberbullying, digital ethics, information literacy and responsible use of artificial intelligence into their guidance and counselling programmes. Confiscation and punishment alone will not solve the problem. Students must be taught self-regulation. Teachers and parents have a responsibility! Teachers should not see the tablet merely as a device to monitor. It should be integrated into teaching through research assignments, electronic textbooks, past questions, educational videos, digital presentations and collaborative learning. Parents and guardians must equally reinforce responsible use at home by establishing reasonable expectations around study, entertainment and sleep. The responsibility therefore rests on government, schools, teachers, counsellors, parents, and students. The next question must be about impact. The government has made a substantial investment in digitalising education. The official objective of the Ghana Smart Schools Project is to use technology to enhance teaching and learning and equip students for a rapidly changing world. The next stage must, therefore, go beyond distribution. We must ask: Are students reading more? Are they researching more? Are students using the devices effectively? Are students becoming more digitally competent? And, ultimately, are learning outcomes improving? These questions should be answered through periodic national evaluations involving classroom observations, learner surveys and analyses of academic performance. The tablet is an opportunity, not a toy We must not demonise technology. Ghanaian students will graduate into a world in which digital competence, information literacy and technological adaptability are essential. Our responsibility is, therefore, not to keep students away from technology but to teach them how to control technology rather than allowing technology to control them. The Free SHS programme has opened the doors of secondary education to more Ghanaian children. The One Student–One Tablet initiative has the potential to open another door to digital learning. But that opportunity will only be realised when students understand that the tablet in their hands is not merely a possession or entertainment device; it is an investment in their education and future. The government has provided the device. The school must provide guidance. The teacher must provide the direction. The counsellor must provide the behavioural support. The parent must provide the reinforcement. The student must provide the discipline. Only then can Ghana move from Free SHS and free tablets to meaningful learning outcomes. Technology transforms education only when it transforms learning habits. The success of the One Student-One Tablet initiative will ultimately depend not on how many devices are distributed but on how wisely they are used. Thank you.

items.title: Mahama has not abandoned Haruna Iddrisu, he is backing him to fix education challenges – Spokesperson
items.description: The spokesperson for the Minister of Education, Haruna Iddrisu, says President John Mahama has not abandoned the Minister to deal with challenges confronting Ghana’s education sector. According to Hashmin Mohammed, claims by former Manhyia North MP, Collins Owusu Amankwah, suggesting that the President had left Mr Iddrisu to struggle with challenges in the sector were “factually wrong, politically convenient and completely unsupported by the evidence”. In a statement, Mr Mohammed said attempts to portray challenges associated with the 2026 Computerised School Selection and Placement System (CSSPS) as evidence of presidential neglect were an effort to create a false political narrative. “The attempt to portray the challenges associated with the 2026 Computerised School Selection and Placement System (CSSPS) as evidence of presidential neglect is nothing more than an attempt to manufacture a political narrative where none exists,” he said. Mr Mohammed maintained that the CSSPS was functioning and undergoing reforms to address longstanding weaknesses and improve the experience of students, parents and schools. He said the Ministry of Education inherited a system that required significant reforms but had chosen to confront the challenges rather than continue blaming previous administrations. “The Hon. Minister has chosen to confront the problems head-on, strengthening the system, improving accountability and putting mechanisms in place to make placement more transparent, responsive and efficient,” he stated. According to him, the decentralisation of placement resolution centres was among the interventions introduced to bring assistance closer to parents and students and reduce the difficulties associated with resolving placement-related concerns. He argued that challenges associated with a complex national placement exercise should not automatically be interpreted as evidence of a lack of government support. Mr Mohammed stressed that President Mahama remained firmly behind Mr Iddrisu and the reforms being undertaken in the education sector. “President John Dramani Mahama did not appoint Hon. Haruna Iddrisu to fail. He appointed him to fix problems. And he is supporting him to do exactly that,” he said. He said the President’s support was reflected in government policies, resource allocation and interventions aimed at transforming the education sector. According to the spokesperson, the government is simultaneously addressing infrastructure deficits, expanding school capacity and improving access to teaching and learning materials. He said the objective was to create sufficient capacity in both Category A and Category B schools to ensure Ghanaian children were not denied access to quality secondary education because of inadequate infrastructure or limited school capacity. Mr Mohammed urged political actors to ensure that discussions surrounding education were based on facts rather than political convenience. “We appreciate the former MP’s interest in Ghana’s education sector. But public discourse on education must be based on facts, not political convenience,” he said. He added that presenting every challenge encountered during the implementation of a national programme as evidence of presidential failure would not contribute to solving the underlying problems. “The reality is that the Mahama administration inherited challenges across the education sector and has chosen to confront them through reform, investment and institutional strengthening,” he stated. Mr Mohammed maintained that the CSSPS was being improved rather than abandoned, while the Education Minister was receiving the necessary support to address challenges in the sector. “The CSSPS is being improved, not abandoned. The Education Minister is being supported, not isolated. And the education sector is being reformed, not left to drift,” he said. He insisted that President Mahama had given Mr Iddrisu the mandate, political backing and institutional support to address the problems he inherited. “Those who have genuine concerns about education are welcome to contribute constructive ideas. But attempts to turn every reform challenge into evidence of presidential abandonment will not change the facts,” he added. “The Government is fixing the system. The reforms are underway. And President Mahama remains firmly behind the Education Minister.”
